-- Both rates are real seconds (anchored to clip start / clip end), so
-- retiming the clip changes only how long the fully typed line holds.

local kSecondsPerType = 0.09 -- typing rate, anchored to the clip start
local kSecondsPerDelete = 0.05 -- backspace rate, anchored to the clip end
local kPopDuration = 0.25 -- seconds each typed character takes to settle
local kPopScale = 0.35 -- overshoot amount at the moment a character lands
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)

    local typedCharacters = ctx.time / kSecondsPerType
    local keepableCharacters = remainingSeconds / kSecondsPerDelete
    local visibleCharacters =
        mt.clamp(math.min(typedCharacters, keepableCharacters), 0.0, characterCount)

    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "character"
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = visibleCharacters / characterCount

    -- Pop-in on the typing edge: scale each character by how long ago it
    -- was typed. During the backspace phase the pop is already settled,
    -- so this only shapes the entrance.
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local secondsSinceTyped = ctx.time - index * kSecondsPerType
        local settle = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(secondsSinceTyped / kPopDuration))
        character.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - settle) * kPopScale
    end
end
description: Showcase: typewriter telop. Characters are typed at a fixed real-time rate from the clip start via ctx.output.write_on_*, and near the clip end they are deleted backspace-style at a slightly faster rate. Each newly typed character also pops in with a small overshoot so the typing edge feels mechanical rather than a flat reveal.

name: 03_pop_bounce.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: variety-show style pop telop. Characters pop in one after
-- another with an elastic overshoot, hold with a gentle synchronized
-- pulse, then shrink away in order while twisting slightly. The stagger
-- runs across the whole line so both the entrance and the exit read as a
-- left-to-right cascade.

local kIntroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.6 -- how much of each window is spread across characters
local kIdlePulseAmount = 0.02 -- scale amplitude of the hold-phase pulse
local kIdlePulseSpeed = 1.2 -- pulses per second during the hold
local kExitTwistDegrees = 25.0 -- rotation each character picks up while leaving

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kStaggerAmount
        local charIntro = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local charOutro = mt.ease.in_back(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        local idlePulse = mt.wave(ctx.time, kIdlePulseSpeed, index * 0.4) * kIdlePulseAmount

        character.scale = charIntro * (1.0 - charOutro) + idlePulse * charIntro
        character.rotation = charOutro * kExitTwistDegrees
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(charIntro * 4.0) * (1.0 - charOutro)
    end
end
description: Showcase: variety-show style pop telop. Characters pop in one after another with an elastic overshoot, hold with a gentle synchronized pulse, then shrink away in order while twisting slightly. The stagger runs across the whole line so both the entrance and the exit read as a left-to-right cascade.

name: 04_tracking_reveal.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: cinematic title reveal. The line starts letterspaced far
-- apart and almost transparent, converges while fading in, keeps drifting
-- apart very slowly during the hold (the classic movie-title tracking
-- creep), then spreads wide again as it fades out.
--
-- Tracking is faked with per-character offset_x: each character is pushed
-- away from the line center proportionally to its distance from it, so
-- the layout itself is never retypeset.

local kIntroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kIntroSpread = 0.12 -- canvas-width fraction the outermost characters start away
local kOutroSpread = 0.10 -- canvas-width fraction the outermost characters end away
local kIdleCreepPerSecond = 0.004 -- slow hold-phase tracking drift, canvas-width fraction

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local introEase = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount)
    local outroEase = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount)

    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local lineCenter = (characterCount + 1) * 0.5

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        -- -1.0 at the left edge of the line, +1.0 at the right edge.
        local centerDistance = 0.0
        if characterCount > 1 then
            centerDistance = (index - lineCenter) / (lineCenter - 1.0)
        end

        local spread = (1.0 - introEase) * kIntroSpread
            + outroEase * kOutroSpread
            + ctx.time * kIdleCreepPerSecond

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + centerDistance * spread
        character.opacity = introEase * (1.0 - outroEase)
    end
end
description: Showcase: cinematic title reveal. The line starts letterspaced far apart and almost transparent, converges while fading in, keeps drifting apart very slowly during the hold (the classic movie-title tracking creep), then spreads wide again as it fades out.

name: 05_wipe_slide.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: left-to-right wipe telop. A soft-edged reveal front sweeps
-- across the canvas at the intro, each character fading in with a small
-- slide as the front passes it; at the outro a second front sweeps the
-- same direction and wipes the line away. The fronts are positional
-- (driven by each character's canvas x position, not its index), so
-- multi-line text wipes as one shape.

local kIntroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kEdgeSoftness = 0.18 -- canvas-width fraction over which the front feathers
local kSlideDistance = 0.03 -- canvas-width fraction each character slides while appearing

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    -- Each front travels from just left of the canvas to just past its
    -- right edge, so the feathered edge fully clears both sides.
    local introFront = -kEdgeSoftness + mt.ease.in_out_sine(introAmount) * (1.0 + 2.0 * kEdgeSoftness)
    local outroFront = -kEdgeSoftness + mt.ease.in_out_sine(outroAmount) * (1.0 + 2.0 * kEdgeSoftness)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local positionX = character.geometry.bounds_center_x

        local revealed = mt.saturate((introFront - positionX) / kEdgeSoftness + 1.0)
        local wiped = mt.saturate((outroFront - positionX) / kEdgeSoftness + 1.0)
        if outroAmount <= 0.0 then
            wiped = 0.0
        end

        character.offset_x = 0.5 - (1.0 - revealed) * kSlideDistance + wiped * kSlideDistance
        character.opacity = revealed * (1.0 - wiped)
    end
end
description: Showcase: left-to-right wipe telop. A soft-edged reveal front sweeps across the canvas at the intro, each character fading in with a small slide as the front passes it; at the outro a second front sweeps the same direction and wipes the line away. The fronts are positional (driven by each character's canvas x position, not its index), so multi-line text wipes as one shape.

name: 06_idle_wobble.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: intro/outro reveal combined with an always-on idle wobble
-- (per-character bob/rotation plus a subtle camera drift).
--
-- Enable "3D Projection" on the inspector to also see the camera drift;
-- without it, the camera writes below are simply ignored.
--
-- Per-character phase uses instance_seed (not OnInitialize arrays):
-- OnInitialize does not expose text / font / char_count / part_count.

local kIntroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.camera.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.05) * 12.0
    ctx.camera.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.04, math.pi / 2.0) * 6.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * 0.5
        local charIntro = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local charOutro = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local visibility = charIntro * (1.0 - charOutro)

        -- Idle loop: a gentle bob and wobble, always running so the held
        -- middle section is not static.
        local phase = mt.random_range(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local idleOffset = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.5, phase) * 0.03
        local idleRotation = mt.noise1(ctx.time * 0.4 + index, 5) * 6.0

        character.offset_y = 0.5 - (1.0 - charIntro) * 0.25 + charOutro * 0.25 + idleOffset
        character.scale = (0.6 + charIntro * 0.4)
        character.rotation = idleRotation

        character.opacity = visibility
    end
end
description: Showcase: intro/outro reveal combined with an always-on idle wobble (per-character bob/rotation plus a subtle camera drift).

name: 07_part_assemble.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: part assemble/burst telop. Every part flies in from its own
-- random direction with its own spin and settles into the glyph; at the
-- outro the parts burst apart along DIFFERENT random directions, so the
-- exit reads as an explosion rather than a reversed entrance.
--
-- Most Latin letters are a single part, so try this with multi-part
-- glyphs (kanji, kana, "%", "=") to see characters visibly self-assemble
-- from separate strokes.
--
-- All per-part randomness is derived from ctx.meta.instance_seed, so it
-- is stable across frames and differs between effect instances.

local kIntroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.5 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kMinScatter = 0.15 -- canvas fraction, shortest fly-in distance
local kMaxScatter = 0.35 -- canvas fraction, longest fly-in distance
local kBurstDistance = 0.45 -- canvas fraction the parts travel while bursting
local kMaxSpinDegrees = 200.0 -- fly-in spin at the fully scattered pose
local kEntryScale = 0.4 -- extra scale while scattered (parts fly in large)

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local stagger = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kStaggerAmount)
        local partIntro = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local partOutro = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        -- Independent random channels are decorrelated by salting the
        -- index with the part count.
        local inAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local outAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 2, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local scatter = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 3, kMinScatter, kMaxScatter)
        local spin = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 4, -kMaxSpinDegrees, kMaxSpinDegrees)

        local flyIn = 1.0 - partIntro
        local burst = partOutro * kBurstDistance

        part.offset_x = 0.5 + math.cos(inAngle) * scatter * flyIn + math.cos(outAngle) * burst
        part.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(inAngle) * scatter * flyIn + math.sin(outAngle) * burst
        part.rotation = spin * flyIn + spin * partOutro
        part.scale = 1.0 + kEntryScale * flyIn
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(partIntro * 3.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(partOutro))
    end
end
description: Showcase: part assemble/burst telop. Every part flies in from its own random direction with its own spin and settles into the glyph; at the outro the parts burst apart along DIFFERENT random directions, so the exit reads as an explosion rather than a reversed entrance.

name: 08_stroke_order_draw.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend lang ja
-- Showcase: handwriting telop. Parts are revealed one by one in stroke
-- order (ctx.output.write_on_mode = "part" with reorder_parts), so kanji
-- appear to be written stroke by stroke; near the clip end the strokes
-- are erased in reverse order at a faster rate. Each stroke also pops
-- slightly as it lands.
--
-- The text is forced to kanji here because stroke order is invisible on
-- single-part Latin letters; swap in your own multi-part text freely.
--
-- The pop timing is approximated from the part's layout index. Inside a
-- multi-part character the actual reveal order is the stroke order, which
-- can differ from layout order, but both fall in the same time window so
-- the approximation is not visible.

local kSecondsPerStroke = 0.14 -- drawing rate, anchored to the clip start
local kSecondsPerErase = 0.07 -- erasing rate, anchored to the clip end
local kPopDuration = 0.3 -- seconds each stroke takes to settle
local kPopScale = 0.25 -- overshoot amount at the moment a stroke lands
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.text = "永字八法"
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local partCount = math.max(ctx.part_count, 1)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)

    local drawnStrokes = ctx.time / kSecondsPerStroke
    local keepableStrokes = remainingSeconds / kSecondsPerErase
    local visibleStrokes = mt.clamp(math.min(drawnStrokes, keepableStrokes), 0.0, partCount)

    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "part"
    ctx.output.reorder_parts = true
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = visibleStrokes / partCount

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local secondsSinceDrawn = ctx.time - index * kSecondsPerStroke
        local settle = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(secondsSinceDrawn / kPopDuration))
        part.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - settle) * kPopScale
    end
end
description: Showcase: handwriting telop. Parts are revealed one by one in stroke order (ctx.output.write_on_mode = "part" with reorder_parts), so kanji appear to be written stroke by stroke; near the clip end the strokes are erased in reverse order at a faster rate. Each stroke also pops slightly as it lands.

name: 09_part_rain.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: falling-parts telop. Parts drop in from above at individually
-- random moments and bounce as they land (out_bounce shapes the whole
-- fall-and-settle in one curve); at the outro the glyphs lose their
-- support and collapse -- every part accelerates straight down while
-- tumbling, exiting below the frame.
--
-- Multi-part glyphs (kanji, kana, "%") make the rain readable as strokes
-- piling up into characters rather than whole letters dropping.

local kIntroDuration = 1.1 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.7 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kDropHeight = 0.25 -- canvas fraction the parts fall from
local kCollapseDistance = 0.6 -- canvas fraction the parts fall past their spot
local kMaxTumbleDegrees = 120.0 -- rotation picked up while collapsing

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local dropDelay = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kStaggerAmount)
        local landing = mt.ease.out_bounce(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + dropDelay) - dropDelay))

        local collapseDelay = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, kStaggerAmount * 0.5)
        local collapse =
            mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + collapseDelay) - collapseDelay))
        local tumble = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 2, -kMaxTumbleDegrees, kMaxTumbleDegrees)

        part.offset_y = 0.5 + (1.0 - landing) * kDropHeight - collapse * kCollapseDistance
        part.rotation = tumble * collapse
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(landing * 4.0)
    end
end
description: Showcase: falling-parts telop. Parts drop in from above at individually random moments and bounce as they land (out_bounce shapes the whole fall-and-settle in one curve); at the outro the glyphs lose their support and collapse -- every part accelerates straight down while tumbling, exiting below the frame.

name: 10_part_swirl.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: swirl telop. Each part spirals inward around its owning
-- character's center -- pushed outward and swept around by an angle that
-- both decay to zero as the intro completes -- then unwinds the OPPOSITE
-- way at the outro so the exit is not a reversed entrance.
--
-- The outward direction comes from part.geometry.local_center (the part's
-- natural position relative to its character's center), so multi-part
-- glyphs bloom open around their own middle. Single-part characters sit
-- exactly on that center, so they fall back to a random direction.

local kIntroDuration = 1.1 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.4 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kSwirlRadius = 0.18 -- canvas fraction the parts are pushed outward
local kSwirlTurns = 0.75 -- revolutions swept while fully unwound
local kCenterEpsilon = 1e-4 -- below this, local_center is treated as zero

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local stagger = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kStaggerAmount)
        local partIntro = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local partOutro = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        -- Unit direction from the character center to this part; random
        -- fallback for single-part characters sitting on the center.
        local localX = part.geometry.local_center_x
        local localY = part.geometry.local_center_y
        local length = math.sqrt(localX * localX + localY * localY)
        local directionAngle
        if length > kCenterEpsilon then
            directionAngle = math.atan(localY, localX)
        else
            directionAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        end

        -- Intro winds clockwise while converging; outro unwinds the other
        -- way while spreading back out.
        local radius = (1.0 - partIntro) * kSwirlRadius + partOutro * kSwirlRadius
        local sweep = (1.0 - partIntro) * kSwirlTurns * math.pi * 2.0
            - partOutro * kSwirlTurns * math.pi * 2.0
        local angle = directionAngle + sweep

        part.offset_x = 0.5 + math.cos(angle) * radius
        part.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(angle) * radius
        part.rotation = math.deg(sweep)
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(partIntro * 3.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(partOutro))
    end
end
description: Showcase: swirl telop. Each part spirals inward around its owning character's center -- pushed outward and swept around by an angle that both decay to zero as the intro completes -- then unwinds the OPPOSITE way at the outro so the exit is not a reversed entrance.

name: 11_part_flip_3d.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: flipboard telop (3D). Parts start edge-on like split-flap
-- tiles and flip to face the camera in a left-to-right cascade, slightly
-- overshooting before settling; at the outro they flip over the OTHER
-- axis (pitch instead of yaw) while sinking away in depth, so the exit
-- reads as the board folding down rather than a reversed entrance.
--
-- part.yaw / part.pitch / part.z are script-only 3D fields: they can be
-- written under any preset, but only render with 3D Projection enabled.

local kIntroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.8 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kEdgeOnDegrees = 90.0 -- yaw/pitch at which a tile is edge-on (invisible)
local kSinkDepth = 0.5 -- z travelled while the board folds away

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.part_count, 1)) * kStaggerAmount
        local flipIn = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local foldOut = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        part.yaw = (1.0 - flipIn) * kEdgeOnDegrees
        part.pitch = foldOut * kEdgeOnDegrees
        part.z = foldOut * kSinkDepth

        -- The edge-on pose is already nearly invisible; the opacity ramp
        -- just hides the sliver of thickness right at the start and end.
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(flipIn * 5.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(foldOut))
    end
end
description: Showcase: flipboard telop (3D). Parts start edge-on like split-flap tiles and flip to face the camera in a left-to-right cascade, slightly overshooting before settling; at the outro they flip over the OTHER axis (pitch instead of yaw) while sinking away in depth, so the exit reads as the board folding down rather than a reversed entrance.

name: 12_depth_dolly.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: depth dolly telop (3D). Characters start deep in the scene
-- (z positive = away from camera), small and faded like distant fog, and
-- dolly forward one after another into the resting plane; at the outro
-- they accelerate PAST the camera (z negative = toward the viewer),
-- growing huge and fading as they fly by.
--
-- Enable "3D Projection" on the inspector; perspective does all the
-- scaling here, so no character.scale is written at all.

local kIntroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.5 -- how much of each window is spread across characters
local kFarDepth = 2.5 -- z at the start of the intro (canvas heights, away)
local kFlyByDepth = -0.8 -- z at the end of the outro (toward / past the camera)

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kStaggerAmount
        local dollyIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local flyBy = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.z = (1.0 - dollyIn) * kFarDepth + flyBy * kFlyByDepth
        character.opacity = dollyIn * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(flyBy))
    end
end
description: Showcase: depth dolly telop (3D). Characters start deep in the scene (z positive = away from camera), small and faded like distant fog, and dolly forward one after another into the resting plane; at the outro they accelerate PAST the camera (z negative = toward the viewer), growing huge and fading as they fly by.

name: 13_hinge_swing.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: hinge telop (3D). Each character is hinged along its BOTTOM
-- edge (pivot_y moved down by half the glyph height): at the intro it
-- lies flat away from the camera (pitch -90, top edge pushed into the
-- scene) and swings upright with a small overshoot; at the outro the
-- characters fall the OPPOSITE way -- toward the viewer, domino-style,
-- left to right -- so the exit is not a reversed entrance.
--
-- Sign convention: positive pitch turns the top edge toward the camera,
-- so lying back is -90 and falling forward is +90.

local kIntroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kIntroStagger = 0.5 -- entrance cascade across characters
local kOutroStagger = 0.8 -- domino cascade across characters
local kHingeDegrees = 90.0 -- pitch magnitude at the flat pose

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))
        local introStagger = order * kIntroStagger
        local outroStagger = order * kOutroStagger

        local standUp =
            mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + introStagger) - introStagger))
        -- Gravity-flavored fall: slow tip, fast slam.
        local fallOver =
            mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + outroStagger) - outroStagger))

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.pitch = -(1.0 - standUp) * kHingeDegrees + fallOver * kHingeDegrees
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(standUp * 3.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(fallOver))
    end
end
description: Showcase: hinge telop (3D). Each character is hinged along its BOTTOM edge (pivot_y moved down by half the glyph height): at the intro it lies flat away from the camera (pitch -90, top edge pushed into the scene) and swings upright with a small overshoot; at the outro the characters fall the OPPOSITE way -- toward the viewer, domino-style, left to right -- so the exit is not a reversed entrance.

name: 14_orbit_reveal.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: camera-driven reveal (3D). The text itself barely moves --
-- the CAMERA does the telop work. It starts far around to the left with
-- strong perspective and pulled back, orbits to a frontal framing while
-- zooming in and relaxing the lens, then leaves around the OTHER side
-- while pulling away, like a crane shot passing a signboard.
--
-- Camera fields are OnPreLayout-only; the per-character stagger fade in
-- OnLayout is the only text-side animation.

local kIntroDuration = 1.4 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kIntroYawDegrees = -65.0 -- camera starts this far around to the left
local kOutroYawDegrees = 55.0 -- camera leaves around the right side
local kIntroPitchDegrees = 14.0 -- slight high angle at the start
local kRestZoom = 1.0
local kIntroZoom = 0.82 -- pulled back at the start
local kOutroZoom = 0.7 -- pulled back further at the end
local kRestPerspective = 0.45
local kAngledPerspective = 0.95 -- lens is widest while the camera is off-axis
local kFadeStagger = 0.4 -- how much of each window is spread across characters

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local arriveEase = mt.ease.in_out_cubic(introAmount)
    local leaveEase = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount)

    ctx.camera.yaw = (1.0 - arriveEase) * kIntroYawDegrees + leaveEase * kOutroYawDegrees
    ctx.camera.pitch = (1.0 - arriveEase) * kIntroPitchDegrees
    ctx.camera.zoom = kIntroZoom + (kRestZoom - kIntroZoom) * arriveEase
        + (kOutroZoom - kRestZoom) * leaveEase
    ctx.camera.perspective = kRestPerspective
        + (kAngledPerspective - kRestPerspective) * ((1.0 - arriveEase) + leaveEase)
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kFadeStagger
        local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        character.opacity = fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end
description: Showcase: camera-driven reveal (3D). The text itself barely moves -- the CAMERA does the telop work. It starts far around to the left with strong perspective and pulled back, orbits to a frontal framing while zooming in and relaxing the lens, then leaves around the OTHER side while pulling away, like a crane shot passing a signboard.

name: 15_vortex_spiral.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: vortex telop (3D). Characters rise out of a deep spiral --
-- each one orbits the line on its own phase while climbing from far away
-- (z positive) to the resting plane, unwinding its spin as it arrives.
-- At the outro the vortex reverses: everything is sucked back into the
-- depth spinning the OTHER way, slightly tighter than it came out.

local kIntroDuration = 1.3 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.45 -- how much of each window is spread across characters
local kVortexDepth = 1.8 -- z at the mouth of the vortex (canvas heights, away)
local kIntroRadius = 0.20 -- canvas fraction of the orbit at full wind-up
local kOutroRadius = 0.12 -- tighter orbit while being sucked back in
local kIntroTurns = 1.0 -- revolutions unwound during the entrance
local kOutroTurns = 0.75 -- revolutions wound up (reversed) during the exit
local kSpinDegrees = 240.0 -- character self-spin at full wind-up

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))
        local stagger = order * kStaggerAmount
        local riseUp = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local suckIn = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        -- Each character orbits on its own phase so the line reads as one
        -- twisting column instead of a rigid ring.
        local phase = order * math.pi * 2.0
        local sweep = (1.0 - riseUp) * kIntroTurns * math.pi * 2.0
            - suckIn * kOutroTurns * math.pi * 2.0
        local radius = (1.0 - riseUp) * kIntroRadius + suckIn * kOutroRadius

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + math.cos(phase + sweep) * radius
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(phase + sweep) * radius
        character.z = (1.0 - riseUp) * kVortexDepth + suckIn * kVortexDepth
        character.rotation = math.deg(sweep) * (kSpinDegrees / 360.0)
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(riseUp * 2.5) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(suckIn))
    end
end
description: Showcase: vortex telop (3D). Characters rise out of a deep spiral -- each one orbits the line on its own phase while climbing from far away (z positive) to the resting plane, unwinding its spin as it arrives. At the outro the vortex reverses: everything is sucked back into the depth spinning the OTHER way, slightly tighter than it came out.

name: 16_stamp_slam.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @required 3d
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: stamp slam telop (3D). Characters drop in from just in front
-- of the camera (z negative = huge) and slam onto the resting plane one
-- after another on a fixed real-time schedule; every impact kicks the
-- camera's lens shift with a short decaying shake, so the whole frame
-- flinches on each hit. At the outro all characters launch back toward
-- the viewer together.
--
-- The slam schedule is index-based real seconds, so OnPreLayout (which
-- has no char_count) can rebuild the same impact times from ctx.text to
-- drive the camera shake in sync with OnLayout's drops.

local kFirstSlamDelay = 0.25 -- seconds before the first character starts falling
local kSlamInterval = 0.15 -- seconds between consecutive characters
local kSlamDuration = 0.22 -- seconds each character takes to fall
local kStartDepth = -0.9 -- z at the start of a drop (toward the camera, huge)
local kSettleTiltDegrees = 12.0 -- random tilt while airborne, straightening on impact
local kShakeDuration = 0.3 -- seconds each impact shake takes to die out
local kShakeAmplitude = 0.012 -- lens-shift peak, canvas fraction
local kShakeFrequency = 22.0 -- shake oscillations per second
local kOutroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kExitDepth = -1.2 -- z at the end of the outro launch
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

local function slamLandTime(index)
    return kFirstSlamDelay + (index - 1) * kSlamInterval + kSlamDuration
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- char_count does not exist yet in this hook; the character count is
    -- approximated from the raw text (close enough for the shake window).
    local characterCount = (utf8 and utf8.len(ctx.text)) or #ctx.text

    local shake = 0.0
    for index = 1, characterCount do
        local sinceImpact = ctx.time - slamLandTime(index)
        if sinceImpact >= 0.0 and sinceImpact < kShakeDuration then
            local decay = (1.0 - sinceImpact / kShakeDuration) ^ 2.0
            shake = shake
                + math.sin(sinceImpact * kShakeFrequency * math.pi * 2.0) * decay * kShakeAmplitude
        end
    end

    ctx.camera.lens_shift_x = shake * 0.5
    ctx.camera.lens_shift_y = shake
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local launch = mt.ease.in_cubic(
        mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kOutroDuration))

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local dropStart = slamLandTime(index) - kSlamDuration
        -- Accelerating fall: the stamp hits hardest at the very end.
        local fall = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate((ctx.time - dropStart) / kSlamDuration))
        local tilt =
            mt.random_range(ctx.meta.instance_seed, index, -kSettleTiltDegrees, kSettleTiltDegrees)

        character.z = (1.0 - fall) * kStartDepth + launch * kExitDepth
        character.rotation = tilt * (1.0 - fall)
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(fall * 4.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(launch))
    end
end
description: Showcase: stamp slam telop (3D). Characters drop in from just in front of the camera (z negative = huge) and slam onto the resting plane one after another on a fixed real-time schedule; every impact kicks the camera's lens shift with a short decaying shake, so the whole frame flinches on each hit. At the outro all characters launch back toward the viewer together.

name: 17_news_flash.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: breaking-news telop. Intro: (1) the bounding box's bottom
-- edge draws itself left-to-right as an underline, (2) the band fill
-- lights up behind it, (3) the text slides on while its tracking
-- converges. Outro reverses the order: text off, band off, then the line
-- retracts toward the RIGHT edge, completing the left-to-right pen path.
--
-- Line-draw technique: a box edge always grows symmetrically from the
-- bounds center (length = text width + 2 * margin_x). Anchoring one END
-- of the edge only needs the margin delta:
--   left-anchored  growth : stroke_offset_x = margin - kBandMarginX
--   right-anchored shrink : stroke_offset_x = kBandMarginX - margin
-- The zero-length start margin is -textWidth/2 in fontSize percent; the
-- em size is approximated as (ascent + descent) * canvas height.

local kLineInDuration = 0.5 -- seconds the underline takes to draw
local kBandInDelay = 0.5 -- seconds before the band fill starts lighting
local kBandInDuration = 0.3
local kTextInDelay = 0.75 -- seconds before the text starts sliding on
local kTextInDuration = 0.5
local kTextOutLead = 1.1 -- seconds before clip end the text starts leaving
local kTextOutDuration = 0.35
local kBandOutDuration = 0.25 -- band-off runs right before the line retracts
local kLineOutLead = 0.45 -- the line retracts over the final stretch
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kBandMarginX = 22.0 -- fontSize percent, final underline overhang
local kBandMarginY = 18.0 -- fontSize percent, band height around the text
local kLineWidth = 6.0 -- fontSize percent
local kBandColor = { r = 0.72, g = 0.05, b = 0.11, a = 1.0 }
local kBandOpacity = 0.9
local kTrackingSpread = 0.04 -- extra tracking while the text is still loose
local kSlideDistance = 0.03 -- canvas fraction the text slides in from
local kTextStagger = 0.4 -- entrance cascade across characters

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.fill.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 0.8
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 45.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.55 }

    local textIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate((ctx.time - kTextInDelay) / kTextInDuration))
    ctx.global.tracking = (1.0 - textIn) * kTrackingSpread
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)

    -- Text bounds width, converted to fontSize percent via the em
    -- approximation, gives the margin at which the edge length is zero.
    local minEdge = math.huge
    local maxEdge = -math.huge
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local geometry = ctx.chars[index].geometry
        minEdge = math.min(minEdge, geometry.bounds_center_x - geometry.bounds_width * 0.5)
        maxEdge = math.max(maxEdge, geometry.bounds_center_x + geometry.bounds_width * 0.5)
    end
    local textWidthPx = math.max(maxEdge - minEdge, 0.0) * ctx.canvas.width
    local fontSizePx = (ctx.font.ascent + ctx.font.descent) * ctx.canvas.height
    local zeroLengthMargin = -textWidthPx / math.max(fontSizePx, 1.0) * 100.0 * 0.5

    local lineIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(ctx.time / kLineInDuration))
    local lineOut = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kLineOutLead))

    local margin
    local lineOffset
    if lineOut > 0.0 then
        -- Right-anchored retraction: the left endpoint sweeps rightward.
        margin = kBandMarginX + (zeroLengthMargin - kBandMarginX) * lineOut
        lineOffset = kBandMarginX - margin
    else
        -- Left-anchored growth: the right endpoint sweeps rightward.
        margin = zeroLengthMargin + (kBandMarginX - zeroLengthMargin) * lineIn
        lineOffset = margin - kBandMarginX
    end

    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_top = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_left = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_right = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_bottom = true
    ctx.bounding_box.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.bounding_box.width = kLineWidth
    ctx.bounding_box.start_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.end_cap = "round"
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_x = margin
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_y = kBandMarginY
    ctx.bounding_box.stroke_offset_x = lineOffset

    -- The band fill spans the full final box regardless of the line
    -- animation (margin_x also stretches it, so it is gated by opacity
    -- instead and only lights up after the line has finished drawing).
    local bandIn = mt.saturate((ctx.time - kBandInDelay) / kBandInDuration)
    local bandOut = mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - kLineOutLead) / kBandOutDuration)
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_color = kBandColor
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_opacity = bandIn * (1.0 - bandOut) * kBandOpacity

    local textInAmount = mt.saturate((ctx.time - kTextInDelay) / kTextInDuration)
    local textOutAmount =
        mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kTextOutLead - kTextOutDuration)) / kTextOutDuration)
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kTextStagger
        local slideIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(textInAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local slideOut = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(textOutAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.offset_x = 0.5 - (1.0 - slideIn) * kSlideDistance + slideOut * kSlideDistance
        character.opacity = slideIn * (1.0 - slideOut)
    end
end
description: Showcase: breaking-news telop. Intro: (1) the bounding box's bottom edge draws itself left-to-right as an underline, (2) the band fill lights up behind it, (3) the text slides on while its tracking converges. Outro reverses the order: text off, band off, then the line retracts toward the RIGHT edge, completing the left-to-right pen path.

name: 18_neon_flicker.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg #0f0f1a
-- Showcase: neon sign telop. The fill is transparent so only the stroke
-- "tube" shows; a same-color shadow at zero distance doubles as a cheap
-- glow. Letters ignite one by one in random order with the erratic
-- fluorescent flicker of a warming tube, shimmer gently while lit, and at
-- the outro the power is cut -- everything goes dark except one brief
-- afterglow blip before the end.
--
-- Unlit letters stay faintly visible (a dark glass tube), so the sign's
-- shape never fully disappears. All flicker is deterministic noise.

local kIgniteWindow = 1.2 -- seconds over which the letters start igniting
local kIgniteDuration = 0.8 -- seconds each letter takes to stabilize
local kFlickerSpeed = 16.0 -- flicker samples per second while warming up
local kShimmerSpeed = 1.4 -- slow brightness shimmer while fully lit
local kPowerCutLead = 0.8 -- seconds before clip end the power dies
local kBlipStart = 0.38 -- afterglow blip window, seconds of remaining time
local kBlipEnd = 0.3
local kUnlitBrightness = 0.06 -- dark-tube brightness when a letter is off
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kHueA = 340.0 -- oklch hue, pink tubes (odd letters)
local kHueB = 200.0 -- oklch hue, cyan tubes (even letters)

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.fill.transparent = true
    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.012
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 0.0
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 0.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local igniteDelay = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kIgniteWindow)
        local warmup = mt.saturate((ctx.time - igniteDelay) / kIgniteDuration)

        -- Warm-up flicker: the tube strikes on and off, staying on more
        -- often as warmup approaches 1; then a gentle shimmer while lit.
        local strike = mt.noise1(ctx.time * kFlickerSpeed + index * 7.3, 11)
        local brightness
        if strike > 1.0 - 2.0 * warmup then
            brightness = 0.45 + 0.55 * warmup
        else
            brightness = kUnlitBrightness
        end
        if warmup >= 1.0 then
            brightness = 1.0 - 0.08 * (0.5 + 0.5 * mt.noise1(ctx.time * kShimmerSpeed + index, 12))
        end

        -- Power cut: dark for the rest of the clip, except one shared
        -- afterglow blip.
        if remainingSeconds < kPowerCutLead then
            brightness = kUnlitBrightness
            if remainingSeconds < kBlipStart and remainingSeconds > kBlipEnd then
                brightness = 0.7
            end
        end

        local hue = kHueA
        if index % 2 == 0 then
            hue = kHueB
        end
        local tubeColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.35 + 0.45 * brightness, 0.09 + 0.13 * brightness, hue)

        character.stroke.use = true
        character.stroke.width = 0.012 + 0.004 * brightness
        character.stroke.gap = 0.0
        character.stroke.color = tubeColor
        character.shadow.use = true
        character.shadow.color = mt.color.with_alpha(tubeColor, 0.55 * brightness)
        character.opacity = 0.3 + 0.7 * brightness
    end
end
description: Showcase: neon sign telop. The fill is transparent so only the stroke "tube" shows; a same-color shadow at zero distance doubles as a cheap glow. Letters ignite one by one in random order with the erratic fluorescent flicker of a warming tube, shimmer gently while lit, and at the outro the power is cut -- everything goes dark except one brief afterglow blip before the end.

name: 19_gold_shine.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: luxury gold telop. A warm gold fill carries a near-white
-- gradient band whose start/end positions sweep across the text on a
-- fixed period -- the classic specular "shine" pass -- framed by a thin
-- dark stroke and a soft drop shadow. The entrance is deliberately slow:
-- tracking converges while the characters fade up; the exit loosens the
-- tracking again and settles down in place. Elegance over energy.

local kIntroDuration = 1.4 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kShinePeriod = 2.4 -- seconds between shine passes
local kShineHalfWidth = 0.16 -- gradient-position half width of the shine band
local kShineAngleDegrees = 24.0 -- shine sweeps slightly off-vertical
local kTrackingSpread = 0.05 -- extra tracking while loose
local kRiseDistance = 0.02 -- canvas fraction of the entrance rise
local kFadeStagger = 0.5 -- entrance/exit cascade across characters
local kGoldFill = { r = 0.82, g = 0.66, b = 0.30, a = 1.0 }
local kShineColor = { r = 1.0, g = 0.96, b = 0.82, a = 1.0 }
local kStrokeColor = { r = 0.32, g = 0.23, b = 0.08, a = 1.0 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local settleIn = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount)
    local loosenOut = mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount)

    ctx.global.fill.color = kGoldFill
    ctx.global.tracking = (1.0 - settleIn) * kTrackingSpread + loosenOut * kTrackingSpread

    -- Shine pass: a narrow bright band rides the gradient positions from
    -- before the text to past it, once per period, forever.
    local shineCenter = mt.cycle(ctx.time, kShinePeriod) * (1.0 + 2.0 * kShineHalfWidth * 2.0)
        - kShineHalfWidth * 2.0
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "oklab"
    ctx.global.gradient.end_color = kShineColor
    ctx.global.gradient.angle = kShineAngleDegrees
    ctx.global.gradient.midpoint = 0.5
    ctx.global.gradient.start_position = shineCenter - kShineHalfWidth
    ctx.global.gradient.end_position = shineCenter + kShineHalfWidth

    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.004
    ctx.global.stroke.color = kStrokeColor
    ctx.global.stroke.order = "fill_over_stroke"
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"

    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.2
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 45.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.05, g = 0.03, b = 0.0, a = 0.35 }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kFadeStagger
        local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.offset_y = 0.5 - (1.0 - fadeIn) * kRiseDistance
        character.opacity = fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end
description: Showcase: luxury gold telop. A warm gold fill carries a near-white gradient band whose start/end positions sweep across the text on a fixed period -- the classic specular "shine" pass -- framed by a thin dark stroke and a soft drop shadow. The entrance is deliberately slow: tracking converges while the characters fade up; the exit loosens the tracking again and settles down in place. Elegance over energy.

name: 20_jelly_pop.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg checkerboard #dddddd
-- Showcase: jelly pop telop. Rainbow-colored characters drop in one by
-- one and land with a full squash-and-stretch: stretched long while
-- falling, squashed flat on impact (bottom-edge pivot so the squash sits
-- on the baseline), then springing back with an elastic wobble. Each
-- character's own shadow alpha doubles as a height cue -- faint while
-- airborne, solid once landed. The outro is a crouch-and-jump straight
-- up off the screen (in_back supplies the crouch for free).

local kDropWindow = 0.9 -- seconds over which the drops are staggered
local kFallDuration = 0.3 -- seconds each character falls
local kDropHeight = 0.22 -- canvas fraction fallen
local kRecoverDuration = 0.6 -- seconds the squash takes to spring back
local kSquashX = 1.45 -- width multiplier at full squash
local kSquashY = 0.55 -- height multiplier at full squash
local kAirStretchX = 0.85 -- width multiplier while falling
local kAirStretchY = 1.2 -- height multiplier while falling
local kJumpLead = 1.0 -- seconds before clip end the jumps start
local kJumpDuration = 0.5 -- seconds each character takes to leave
local kJumpStagger = 0.4 -- exit cascade across characters
local kJumpHeight = 0.5 -- canvas fraction jumped
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kHueSpread = 0.9 -- fraction of the hue wheel across the line

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- The per-character shadow colors below only recolor the shadow; the
    -- shadow itself must be enabled globally.
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.4
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 90.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local jumpAmount = mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kJumpLead - kJumpDuration)) / kJumpDuration)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))

        local dropStart = order * kDropWindow
        local fall = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate((ctx.time - dropStart) / kFallDuration))
        local sinceLanding = ctx.time - (dropStart + kFallDuration)
        local recover = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(sinceLanding / kRecoverDuration))

        local stretchX
        local stretchY
        if sinceLanding >= 0.0 then
            stretchX = kSquashX + (1.0 - kSquashX) * recover
            stretchY = kSquashY + (1.0 - kSquashY) * recover
        else
            stretchX = kAirStretchX
            stretchY = kAirStretchY
        end

        local jumpStagger = order * kJumpStagger
        local jump = mt.ease.in_back(mt.saturate(jumpAmount * (1.0 + jumpStagger) - jumpStagger))
        local jumpFade = mt.saturate(jumpAmount * (1.0 + jumpStagger) - jumpStagger)

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + (1.0 - fall) * kDropHeight + jump * kJumpHeight
        character.stretch_x = stretchX
        character.stretch_y = stretchY
        character.opacity = fall * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(jumpFade))

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(order * kHueSpread, 0.72, 1.0, 1.0)
        -- Height cue: the contact shadow only darkens once the character
        -- has actually landed.
        character.shadow.use = true
        character.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.1 + 0.35 * fall }
    end
end
description: Showcase: jelly pop telop. Rainbow-colored characters drop in one by one and land with a full squash-and-stretch: stretched long while falling, squashed flat on impact (bottom-edge pivot so the squash sits on the baseline), then springing back with an elastic wobble. Each character's own shadow alpha doubles as a height cue -- faint while airborne, solid once landed. The outro is a crouch-and-jump straight up off the screen (in_back supplies the crouch for free).

name: 21_vertical_ink.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 12
-- @recommend lang ja pos 0.5 0.85 bg #aabbcc
-- Showcase: vertical brush-writing telop. The text is set vertically
-- (columns, top-aligned) and written stroke by stroke in stroke order via
-- the part write-on. Each freshly drawn stroke starts as wet, near-black
-- ink slightly swollen on the page, then dries toward a settled sumi
-- gray over about a second (mt.color.lerp). The outro is a mist fade:
-- the columns drift softly upward and dissolve in writing order.
--
-- The drying timing uses the part's layout index as an approximation of
-- its reveal time (same caveat as 08_stroke_order_draw.lua).
--
-- The writing rate is fixed real seconds, but if the clip is too short
-- to finish all strokes before the mist fade, the rate is compressed so
-- the full text is always written (same pattern as 02_typewriter.lua).

local kSecondsPerStroke = 0.13 -- preferred writing rate, anchored to the clip start
local kFinishedHold = 0.4 -- seconds the completed text should at least hold
local kDryDuration = 1.1 -- seconds a stroke takes to dry
local kWetSwell = 0.07 -- extra scale while the ink is wet
local kMistLead = 1.0 -- seconds before clip end the mist fade starts
local kMistDuration = 0.6 -- seconds each character takes to dissolve
local kMistStagger = 0.5 -- dissolve cascade in writing order
local kMistRise = 0.04 -- canvas fraction drifted upward while dissolving
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kWetInk = { r = 0.04, g = 0.04, b = 0.09, a = 1.0 }
local kDriedInk = { r = 0.22, g = 0.22, b = 0.26, a = 1.0 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.text = "花鳥風月\n山紫水明"
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
    ctx.global.h_align = "center"
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.15
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local partCount = math.max(ctx.part_count, 1)

    -- Compress the writing rate only when the clip cannot fit every
    -- stroke before the mist fade (plus a short hold on the full text).
    local clipLength = kFallbackClipLength
    if ctx.timeline.available then
        clipLength = ctx.timeline.duration_seconds
    end
    local writingBudget = math.max(clipLength - kMistLead - kFinishedHold, kFinishedHold)
    local secondsPerStroke = math.min(kSecondsPerStroke, writingBudget / partCount)

    local writtenStrokes = mt.clamp(ctx.time / secondsPerStroke, 0.0, partCount)

    ctx.output.write_on_mode = "part"
    ctx.output.reorder_parts = true
    ctx.output.write_on_start = 0.0
    ctx.output.write_on_end = writtenStrokes / partCount

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local sinceDrawn = ctx.time - index * secondsPerStroke
        local dried = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(sinceDrawn / kDryDuration))

        part.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - dried) * kWetSwell
        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(kWetInk, kDriedInk, dried)
    end

    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local mistAmount =
        mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kMistLead - kMistDuration)) / kMistDuration)
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kMistStagger
        local dissolve = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(mistAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + dissolve * kMistRise
        character.opacity = 1.0 - dissolve
    end
end
description: Showcase: vertical brush-writing telop. The text is set vertically (columns, top-aligned) and written stroke by stroke in stroke order via the part write-on. Each freshly drawn stroke starts as wet, near-black ink slightly swollen on the page, then dries toward a settled sumi gray over about a second (mt.color.lerp). The outro is a mist fade: the columns drift softly upward and dissolve in writing order.

name: 22_jelly_slide.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: jelly slide telop. Sibling of 20_jelly_pop.lua with the
-- inertia turned sideways: characters shoot in from the left, stretched
-- long by their own speed, and brake hard against their resting spot --
-- squashing along X against a leading-edge pivot before wobbling back.
-- The outro launches them out to the RIGHT, with an in_back anticipation
-- (a small backward lean) and a speed stretch as they leave.

local kSlideWindow = 0.7 -- seconds over which the arrivals are staggered
local kSlideDuration = 0.28 -- seconds each character travels
local kSlideDistance = 0.35 -- canvas fraction travelled in
local kSpeedStretchX = 1.35 -- elongation while flying
local kSpeedStretchY = 0.88
local kBrakeSquashX = 0.6 -- width multiplier at the hardest brake
local kBrakeStretchY = 1.25 -- matching vertical bulge
local kRecoverDuration = 0.55 -- seconds the brake squash takes to spring back
local kExitLead = 1.0 -- seconds before clip end the launches start
local kExitDuration = 0.45 -- seconds each character takes to leave
local kExitStagger = 0.4 -- exit cascade across characters
local kExitDistance = 0.5 -- canvas fraction launched out
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kHueSpread = 0.9 -- fraction of the hue wheel across the line

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local exitAmount =
        mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kExitLead - kExitDuration)) / kExitDuration)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))

        local slideStart = order * kSlideWindow
        local approach = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate((ctx.time - slideStart) / kSlideDuration))
        local sinceBrake = ctx.time - (slideStart + kSlideDuration)
        local recover = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(sinceBrake / kRecoverDuration))

        local stretchX
        local stretchY
        if sinceBrake >= 0.0 then
            stretchX = kBrakeSquashX + (1.0 - kBrakeSquashX) * recover
            stretchY = kBrakeStretchY + (1.0 - kBrakeStretchY) * recover
        else
            stretchX = kSpeedStretchX
            stretchY = kSpeedStretchY
        end

        local exitStagger = order * kExitStagger
        local launchProgress = mt.saturate(exitAmount * (1.0 + exitStagger) - exitStagger)
        local launch = mt.ease.in_back(launchProgress)

        -- The mass piles up against the direction of travel: brake squash
        -- compresses toward the leading (right) edge.
        character.pivot_x = 0.5 + character.geometry.bounds_width * 0.5
        character.offset_x = 0.5 - (1.0 - approach) * kSlideDistance + launch * kExitDistance
        character.stretch_x = stretchX + math.max(launch, 0.0) * 0.4
        character.stretch_y = stretchY
        character.opacity = approach * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(launchProgress))

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(order * kHueSpread, 0.72, 1.0, 1.0)
    end
end
description: Showcase: jelly slide telop. Sibling of 20_jelly_pop.lua with the inertia turned sideways: characters shoot in from the left, stretched long by their own speed, and brake hard against their resting spot -- squashing along X against a leading-edge pivot before wobbling back. The outro launches them out to the RIGHT, with an in_back anticipation (a small backward lean) and a speed stretch as they leave.

name: 23_jelly_bounce.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg checkerboard #dddddd
-- Showcase: multi-bounce jelly telop. Sibling of 20_jelly_pop.lua that
-- does not settle on the first landing: each character falls and takes
-- three decaying bounces, squashing on every contact (impulse decays
-- with the impact) and stretching slightly while airborne. The contact
-- shadow darkens on the ground and fades at the top of each arc. The
-- outro pulls the floor away: a brief startled wobble, then everything
-- tumbles off the bottom of the frame.
--
-- The trajectory is built segment by segment (one fall + one parabola
-- per bounce) instead of a single out_bounce ease, so the squash and the
-- shadow can key off the exact contact times.

local kDropWindow = 0.8 -- seconds over which the drops are staggered
local kFallDuration = 0.3 -- seconds of the initial fall
local kDropHeight = 0.22 -- canvas fraction of the initial fall
local kBounceHeightDecay = 0.42 -- height multiplier per bounce
local kBounceTimeDecay = 0.65 -- duration multiplier per bounce
local kBounceCount = 3
local kFirstBounceDuration = 0.4 -- seconds of the first up-and-down arc
local kSquashImpulse = 0.5 -- stretch delta at the first (hardest) contact
local kSquashRecover = 0.22 -- seconds each contact squash takes to relax
local kAirStretch = 0.12 -- vertical elongation while airborne
local kFloorDropLead = 1.0 -- seconds before clip end the floor vanishes
local kWobbleDuration = 0.25 -- startled wobble before the fall
local kFloorFallDistance = 0.7 -- canvas fraction fallen off screen
local kTumbleDegrees = 100.0 -- max tumble while falling off
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kHueSpread = 0.9 -- fraction of the hue wheel across the line

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.4
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 90.0
end

-- Returns the normalized height (0 = floor), the time since the most
-- recent floor contact (negative before the first landing), and that
-- contact's impact strength (1 = first landing, decaying afterward).
local function bounceState(sequenceTime)
    local height = 1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(sequenceTime / kFallDuration))
    local sinceContact = sequenceTime - kFallDuration
    local impact = 1.0

    local segmentStart = kFallDuration
    local arcDuration = kFirstBounceDuration
    local arcHeight = kBounceHeightDecay
    for _ = 1, kBounceCount do
        if sequenceTime > segmentStart then
            local arcProgress = mt.saturate((sequenceTime - segmentStart) / arcDuration)
            height = arcHeight * 4.0 * arcProgress * (1.0 - arcProgress)
            if arcProgress >= 1.0 then
                sinceContact = sequenceTime - (segmentStart + arcDuration)
                impact = impact * kBounceHeightDecay
            end
        end
        segmentStart = segmentStart + arcDuration
        arcDuration = arcDuration * kBounceTimeDecay
        arcHeight = arcHeight * kBounceHeightDecay
    end
    return height, sinceContact, impact
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local floorGone = mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kFloorDropLead)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local sequenceTime = ctx.time - order * kDropWindow
        local height, sinceContact, impact = bounceState(math.max(sequenceTime, 0.0))
        local appeared = mt.saturate(sequenceTime / 0.05)

        local squash = 0.0
        if sinceContact >= 0.0 then
            local relax = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(sinceContact / kSquashRecover))
            squash = kSquashImpulse * impact * (1.0 - relax)
        end
        local airStretch = kAirStretch * mt.saturate(height * 4.0)

        -- Outro: a short shiver, then the drop through the vanished floor.
        local wobble = 0.0
        if floorGone > 0.0 then
            wobble = mt.noise1(ctx.time * 30.0 + index * 3.7, 21)
                * mt.saturate(floorGone / (kWobbleDuration / kFloorDropLead)) * 3.0
        end
        local plunge = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate((floorGone - kWobbleDuration / kFloorDropLead)
            / (1.0 - kWobbleDuration / kFloorDropLead)))
        local tumble = mt.random_range(seed, index, -kTumbleDegrees, kTumbleDegrees)

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + height * kDropHeight - plunge * kFloorFallDistance
        character.stretch_x = 1.0 + squash - airStretch * 0.5
        character.stretch_y = 1.0 - squash + airStretch
        character.rotation = wobble + tumble * plunge
        character.opacity = appeared * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(plunge))

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(order * kHueSpread, 0.72, 1.0, 1.0)
        character.shadow.use = true
        character.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = (0.1 + 0.35 * (1.0 - height)) * appeared }
    end
end
description: Showcase: multi-bounce jelly telop. Sibling of 20_jelly_pop.lua that does not settle on the first landing: each character falls and takes three decaying bounces, squashing on every contact (impulse decays with the impact) and stretching slightly while airborne. The contact shadow darkens on the ground and fades at the top of each arc. The outro pulls the floor away: a brief startled wobble, then everything tumbles off the bottom of the frame.

name: 24_balloon_pop.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: balloon telop. Sibling of 20_jelly_pop.lua with no gravity
-- at all: characters inflate from nothing with an elastic wobble (the
-- stretch axes run on opposite phases, so they bulge like a soft
-- balloon), then drift and sway while they float. At the outro each one
-- over-inflates for a beat and BURSTS -- a sharp scale spike, a random
-- rotation kick, and gone within a few frames, cascading down the line.

local kInflateWindow = 0.8 -- seconds over which the inflations are staggered
local kInflateDuration = 0.7 -- seconds each balloon takes to inflate
local kWobbleAmount = 0.06 -- opposing stretch amplitude while floating
local kWobbleSpeed = 1.6 -- wobble cycles per second
local kFloatAmount = 0.012 -- canvas fraction of the idle drift
local kFloatSpeed = 0.5 -- drift cycles per second
local kFirstPopLead = 1.0 -- seconds of remaining time when the first balloon pops
local kPopSpread = 0.6 -- seconds between the first and last pop
local kSwellDuration = 0.3 -- seconds of over-inflation before the burst
local kSwellAmount = 0.22 -- extra scale at the moment of bursting
local kBurstDuration = 0.07 -- seconds from burst to fully gone
local kBurstScale = 0.5 -- extra scale spike while bursting
local kBurstKickDegrees = 40.0 -- max rotation kick on burst
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kHueSpread = 0.9 -- fraction of the hue wheel across the line

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local inflateStart = order * kInflateWindow
        local inflate =
            mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate((ctx.time - inflateStart) / kInflateDuration))

        -- Soft-body wobble: X and Y breathe against each other.
        local wobblePhase = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local wobble = mt.wave(ctx.time, kWobbleSpeed, wobblePhase) * kWobbleAmount
        local sway = mt.wave(ctx.time, kFloatSpeed, wobblePhase) * kFloatAmount
        local bob = mt.wave(ctx.time, kFloatSpeed * 1.3, wobblePhase + math.pi / 2.0) * kFloatAmount

        -- Pop schedule, expressed in remaining time so it hugs the clip
        -- end: pre-swell approaches 1 right at the pop moment, then the
        -- burst window takes over.
        local popMoment = kFirstPopLead + kPopSpread - order * kPopSpread
        local sincePop = popMoment - remainingSeconds
        local preSwell = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(1.0 + sincePop / kSwellDuration))
        local burst = mt.saturate(sincePop / kBurstDuration)
        local kick = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.char_count, -kBurstKickDegrees, kBurstKickDegrees)

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + sway
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + bob
        character.scale = inflate * (1.0 + preSwell * kSwellAmount + burst * kBurstScale)
        character.stretch_x = 1.0 + wobble
        character.stretch_y = 1.0 - wobble
        character.rotation = wobble * 60.0 + kick * burst
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(inflate * 2.0) * (1.0 - burst)

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(order * kHueSpread, 0.55, 1.0, 1.0)
    end
end
description: Showcase: balloon telop. Sibling of 20_jelly_pop.lua with no gravity at all: characters inflate from nothing with an elastic wobble (the stretch axes run on opposite phases, so they bulge like a soft balloon), then drift and sway while they float. At the outro each one over-inflates for a beat and BURSTS -- a sharp scale spike, a random rotation kick, and gone within a few frames, cascading down the line.

name: 25_heavy_metal.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg #ccbbaa
-- Showcase: heavy metal telop. Steel plates slam down from above and
-- stop DEAD -- no bounce, no overshoot, no wobble; the rigidity IS the
-- material. Each impact makes the whole line sink for a few frames. The
-- finish is a steel gradient with a fast, narrow specular sweep, a dark
-- edge stroke, and a hard drop shadow. The outro is mechanical: each
-- plate snaps 90 degrees flat around its bottom edge, one after another,
-- like a press folding shut.

local kDropWindow = 0.8 -- seconds over which the slams are staggered
local kDropDuration = 0.2 -- seconds each plate falls (accelerating, no ease-out)
local kDropHeight = 0.3 -- canvas fraction fallen
local kImpactDip = 0.008 -- canvas fraction the whole line sinks per impact
local kImpactDuration = 0.09 -- seconds the sink lasts
local kSnapLead = 1.0 -- seconds before clip end the fold-down starts
local kSnapDuration = 0.12 -- seconds each plate takes to snap flat
local kSnapStagger = 0.7 -- fold cascade across characters
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kShinePeriod = 1.8 -- seconds between specular sweeps
local kShineHalfWidth = 0.07 -- narrow, hard highlight band
local kSteelFill = { r = 0.58, g = 0.62, b = 0.68, a = 1.0 }
local kShineColor = { r = 0.95, g = 0.97, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
local kEdgeColor = { r = 0.1, g = 0.11, b = 0.14, a = 1.0 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.fill.color = kSteelFill

    local shineCenter = mt.cycle(ctx.time, kShinePeriod) * (1.0 + 4.0 * kShineHalfWidth)
        - kShineHalfWidth * 2.0
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "oklab"
    ctx.global.gradient.end_color = kShineColor
    ctx.global.gradient.angle = 18.0
    ctx.global.gradient.midpoint = 0.5
    ctx.global.gradient.start_position = shineCenter - kShineHalfWidth
    ctx.global.gradient.end_position = shineCenter + kShineHalfWidth

    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.005
    ctx.global.stroke.color = kEdgeColor
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "miter_clip" -- hard corners for the machined edge

    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.2
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 90.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.6 }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local snapAmount =
        mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kSnapLead - kSnapDuration)) / kSnapDuration)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)

    -- Every landing shakes the whole line: collect the strongest active
    -- impact dip before styling the characters.
    local lineDip = 0.0
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local landTime = mt.distribute(index, characterCount) * kDropWindow + kDropDuration
        local sinceImpact = ctx.time - landTime
        if sinceImpact >= 0.0 and sinceImpact < kImpactDuration then
            lineDip = math.max(lineDip, kImpactDip * (1.0 - sinceImpact / kImpactDuration))
        end
    end

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)

        local dropStart = order * kDropWindow
        -- Pure acceleration, cut off at the floor: rigid, zero restitution.
        local fall = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate((ctx.time - dropStart) / kDropDuration))

        local snapStagger = order * kSnapStagger
        local snapProgress = mt.saturate(snapAmount * (1.0 + snapStagger) - snapStagger)
        -- Fold-flat is faked in 2D by collapsing the height against the
        -- bottom edge (an edge-on plate), since pitch only renders in 3D.
        local snap = mt.ease.in_quad(snapProgress)

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + (1.0 - fall) * kDropHeight - lineDip
        character.stretch_y = 1.0 - snap * 0.98
        character.opacity = fall * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(snapProgress * 1.2 - 0.2)))
    end
end
description: Showcase: heavy metal telop. Steel plates slam down from above and stop DEAD -- no bounce, no overshoot, no wobble; the rigidity IS the material. Each impact makes the whole line sink for a few frames. The finish is a steel gradient with a fast, narrow specular sweep, a dark edge stroke, and a hard drop shadow. The outro is mechanical: each plate snaps 90 degrees flat around its bottom edge, one after another, like a press folding shut.

name: 26_wood_blocks.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg #aaccaa
-- Showcase: wooden blocks telop. Characters are set down one by one like
-- toy blocks placed by hand: a short decelerating descent (nothing like a
-- fall), then a single small tilt that settles with the faintest clatter
-- overshoot -- wood absorbs energy, so nothing ever springs. Each block
-- gets its own wood-brown tone with a pale birch stroke as the end grain.
-- The outro tips the blocks forward off their bottom edge, and each one
-- clatters briefly (out_bounce on the rotation) as it lands flat.

local kPlaceWindow = 1.0 -- seconds over which the blocks are placed
local kPlaceDuration = 0.3 -- seconds each block takes to be set down
local kPlaceHeight = 0.07 -- canvas fraction, the gentle set-down height
local kSettleTiltDegrees = 5.0 -- initial lean that settles after placement
local kSettleDuration = 0.4 -- seconds the lean takes to settle
local kTipLead = 1.1 -- seconds before clip end the tipping starts
local kTipDuration = 0.5 -- seconds each block takes to tip flat
local kTipStagger = 0.7 -- tipping cascade across characters
local kTipDegrees = 84.0 -- final tipped-over angle
local kFadeAfterTip = 0.3 -- fade applied once a block lies flat
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kWoodTones = {
    { r = 0.55, g = 0.36, b = 0.20, a = 1.0 },
    { r = 0.42, g = 0.27, b = 0.15, a = 1.0 },
    { r = 0.63, g = 0.44, b = 0.26, a = 1.0 },
    { r = 0.49, g = 0.33, b = 0.19, a = 1.0 },
}
local kGrainColor = { r = 0.87, g = 0.78, b = 0.62, a = 1.0 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.008
    ctx.global.stroke.color = kGrainColor
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.0
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 85.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.15, g = 0.09, b = 0.04, a = 0.3 }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local tipAmount =
        mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - (kTipLead - kTipDuration)) / kTipDuration)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1))
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local placeStart = order * kPlaceWindow
        -- Decelerating descent: the block is set down, not dropped.
        local setDown = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate((ctx.time - placeStart) / kPlaceDuration))
        local sincePlaced = ctx.time - (placeStart + kPlaceDuration)
        -- The only springiness in the whole material: a subdued back ease
        -- on the settling lean, never on the position.
        local settle = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate(sincePlaced / kSettleDuration))
        local lean = mt.random_range(seed, index, -kSettleTiltDegrees, kSettleTiltDegrees)

        local tipStagger = order * kTipStagger
        local tipProgress = mt.saturate(tipAmount * (1.0 + tipStagger) - tipStagger)
        local tip = mt.ease.out_bounce(tipProgress) -- wooden clatter at the end of the tip

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + (1.0 - setDown) * kPlaceHeight
        character.rotation = lean * (1.0 - settle) + tip * kTipDegrees
        character.opacity = setDown
            * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate((tipProgress - (1.0 - kFadeAfterTip)) / kFadeAfterTip)))

        local toneIndex = math.floor(mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.char_count, 1.0, #kWoodTones + 0.999))
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = kWoodTones[math.min(toneIndex, #kWoodTones)]
    end
end
