Characters are set down one by one like toy blocks placed by hand: a short decelerating descent (nothing like a fall), then a single small tilt that settles with the faintest clatter overshoot -- wood absorbs energy, so nothing ever springs. Each block gets its own wood-brown tone with a pale birch stroke as the end grain. The outro tips the blocks forward off their bottom edge, and each one clatters briefly (out_bounce on the rotation) as it lands flat.

name: 27_cosmic_dust.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: cosmic dust telop. Parts drift in from deep space as motes
-- of stardust: a slow convergence with a noise wander that dies away as
-- each mote docks into its glyph. Color slides around the violet-blue-
-- cyan band of oklch, drifting with both position and time, and a
-- deterministic sparkle occasionally spikes a mote's lightness and glow
-- (same-color zero-distance shadow). The outro scatters everything back
-- into dust along new directions, sparkling harder as it dissolves.

local kIntroDuration = 1.6 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.3 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.5 -- how much of each window is spread across parts
local kMinDrift = 0.15 -- canvas fraction, shortest drift-in distance
local kMaxDrift = 0.32 -- canvas fraction, longest drift-in distance
local kWanderAmount = 0.02 -- canvas fraction of the residual noise wander
local kWanderSpeed = 0.8 -- wander cycles per second
local kBaseHue = 265.0 / 360.0 -- normalized oklch hue, violet
local kHueSwing = 70.0 / 360.0 -- swings down toward cyan
local kHueDriftSpeed = 0.12 -- hue cycles per second
local kSparkleSpeed = 5.0 -- sparkle noise samples per second
local kSparkleSharpness = 3.0 -- higher = rarer, sharper glints

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.0
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 0.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

        local stagger = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, kStaggerAmount)
        local dock = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local scatter = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        local inAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local outAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 2, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local drift = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 3, kMinDrift, kMaxDrift)

        -- The wander never fully dies during the hold -- stardust floats.
        local loose = math.max(1.0 - dock, scatter)
        local wanderStrength = kWanderAmount * (0.15 + 0.85 * loose)
        local wanderX = mt.noise1(ctx.time * kWanderSpeed + index * 2.13, 31) * wanderStrength
        local wanderY = mt.noise1(ctx.time * kWanderSpeed + index * 2.13, 32) * wanderStrength

        part.offset_x = 0.5 + math.cos(inAngle) * drift * (1.0 - dock)
            + math.cos(outAngle) * drift * scatter + wanderX
        part.offset_y = 0.5 + math.sin(inAngle) * drift * (1.0 - dock)
            + math.sin(outAngle) * drift * scatter + wanderY

        -- Sparkle: sharpened positive noise, boosted while dissolving.
        local glint = math.max(mt.noise1(ctx.time * kSparkleSpeed + index * 4.7, 33), 0.0)
            ^ kSparkleSharpness
        local sparkle = glint * (1.0 + scatter * 1.5)

        local hue = kBaseHue - kHueSwing
            * (0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(index * 0.7 + ctx.time * kHueDriftSpeed * math.pi * 2.0))
        local dustColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.68 + 0.27 * mt.saturate(sparkle), 0.11, hue)

        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = dustColor
        part.shadow.use = true
        part.shadow.color = mt.color.with_alpha(dustColor, 0.35 + 0.45 * mt.saturate(sparkle))
        part.scale = 0.9 + 0.1 * dock + 0.15 * mt.saturate(sparkle)
        part.opacity = mt.saturate(dock * 2.5) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(scatter))
    end
end

Color slides around the violet-blue- cyan band of oklch, drifting with both position and time, and a deterministic sparkle occasionally spikes a mote's lightness and glow (same-color zero-distance shadow). The outro scatters everything back into dust along new directions, sparkling harder as it dissolves.

name: 28_mono_cut.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg #dddddd
-- Showcase: monochrome jump-cut telop. Pure black and white, and NO
-- easing anywhere: time is quantized into hard cuts (kCutsPerSecond) and
-- every value snaps between poses -- the strobe stiffness is the whole
-- aesthetic. The band (bounding box fill) guarantees contrast on any
-- background: the resting pose is a black band with white text, and on
-- flash cuts the whole frame inverts to a white band with black text.
-- Intro: a burst of negative flashes with random character dropouts.
-- Hold: subtle per-cut jitter and a rare single-cut blink. Outro: a
-- second flash burst, then characters vanish one cut at a time.
--
-- All randomness is keyed on (cut index, character index), so each cut
-- holds one deterministic pose -- pause on any frame and it is a poster.

local kCutsPerSecond = 12.0
local kIntroFlashSeconds = 0.7 -- duration of the opening flash burst
local kIntroDropoutChance = 0.35 -- chance a character is missing during a flash cut
local kHoldBlinkChance = 0.06 -- chance a hold-phase cut inverts for one cut
local kJitterAmount = 0.004 -- canvas fraction of the per-cut pose jitter
local kScaleSnapAmount = 0.05 -- per-cut scale snap range
local kOutroFlashLead = 0.9 -- seconds before clip end the closing burst starts
local kVanishLead = 0.45 -- seconds before clip end the characters start vanishing
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kBandMargin = 16.0 -- fontSize percent
local kBlack = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 1.0 }
local kWhite = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local cutIndex = math.floor(ctx.time * kCutsPerSecond)

    -- Phase flags for THIS cut.
    local inIntroBurst = ctx.time < kIntroFlashSeconds
    local inOutroBurst = remainingSeconds < kOutroFlashLead
    local cutRandom = mt.random_range(seed, cutIndex, 0.0, 1.0)

    local inverted = false
    if inIntroBurst or inOutroBurst then
        inverted = cutRandom > 0.5
    elseif cutRandom < kHoldBlinkChance then
        inverted = true
    end

    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_top = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_bottom = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_left = false
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_right = false
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_x = kBandMargin
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_y = kBandMargin * 0.7
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_opacity = 1.0
    local bandColor = kBlack
    local textColor = kWhite
    if inverted then
        bandColor = kWhite
        textColor = kBlack
    end
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_color = bandColor

    -- Vanish phase: fewer characters survive each cut, in a fixed
    -- deterministic shuffle.
    local vanishProgress = mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kVanishLead)
    local visibleCount = math.ceil((1.0 - vanishProgress) * ctx.char_count)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local poseSalt = index * 8191 + cutIndex

        local dropped = false
        if inIntroBurst and mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt + 3, 0.0, 1.0) < kIntroDropoutChance then
            dropped = true
        end
        local vanishRank = math.floor(mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.char_count * 7, 0.0, 0.999)
            * ctx.char_count) + 1
        if vanishProgress > 0.0 and vanishRank > visibleCount then
            dropped = true
        end

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt, -kJitterAmount, kJitterAmount)
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt + 1, -kJitterAmount, kJitterAmount)
        character.scale = 1.0 + mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt + 2, -kScaleSnapAmount, kScaleSnapAmount)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = textColor
        character.opacity = dropped and 0.0 or 1.0
    end
end
description: Showcase: monochrome jump-cut telop. Pure black and white, and NO easing anywhere: time is quantized into hard cuts (kCutsPerSecond) and every value snaps between poses -- the strobe stiffness is the whole aesthetic. The band (bounding box fill) guarantees contrast on any background: the resting pose is a black band with white text, and on flash cuts the whole frame inverts to a white band with black text. Intro: a burst of negative flashes with random character dropouts. Hold: subtle per-cut jitter and a rare single-cut blink. Outro: a second flash burst, then characters vanish one cut at a time.

name: 29_fruit_cut.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend bg #dddddd
-- Showcase: fruit jump-cut telop. Sibling of 28_mono_cut.lua: the exact
-- same quantized-cut grammar (no easing, one deterministic pose per cut),
-- but the palette swaps from black-and-white to juicy fruit colors --
-- lemon, strawberry, lime, orange, grape, blueberry -- cycling one fruit
-- forward on every cut, over a thick white candy stroke and a soft
-- same-hue shadow. Intro: characters pop in over the first few cuts in
-- random order. Outro: they are picked off one cut at a time, with a
-- little scale pop on the cut before each one disappears.

local kCutsPerSecond = 12.0
local kPopInSeconds = 0.6 -- duration of the pop-in phase
local kJitterAmount = 0.004 -- canvas fraction of the per-cut pose jitter
local kScaleSnapAmount = 0.06 -- per-cut scale snap range
local kRotationSnapDegrees = 4.0 -- per-cut rotation snap range
local kVanishLead = 0.8 -- seconds before clip end the picking starts
local kPrePickScale = 1.18 -- scale pop on the cut before a character is picked
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kFruits = {
    { r = 1.0, g = 0.85, b = 0.2, a = 1.0 }, -- lemon
    { r = 0.95, g = 0.25, b = 0.35, a = 1.0 }, -- strawberry
    { r = 0.55, g = 0.85, b = 0.3, a = 1.0 }, -- lime
    { r = 1.0, g = 0.6, b = 0.15, a = 1.0 }, -- orange
    { r = 0.6, g = 0.4, b = 0.85, a = 1.0 }, -- grape
    { r = 0.3, g = 0.5, b = 0.9, a = 1.0 }, -- blueberry
}

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.stroke.width = 0.012
    ctx.global.stroke.color = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
    ctx.global.stroke.join = "round"
    ctx.global.stroke.order = "fill_over_stroke"
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.2
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 60.0
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local cutIndex = math.floor(ctx.time * kCutsPerSecond)

    local popInProgress = mt.saturate(ctx.time / kPopInSeconds)
    local vanishProgress = mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kVanishLead)
    local visibleCount = math.ceil((1.0 - vanishProgress) * ctx.char_count)
    local nextVanishCount = math.ceil(
        (1.0 - mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - 1.0 / kCutsPerSecond) / kVanishLead))
            * ctx.char_count)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local poseSalt = index * 8191 + cutIndex

        -- Pop-in: each character has a fixed random threshold; it exists
        -- once the intro progress passes it (so the fill-in order is a
        -- deterministic shuffle, one deterministic subset per cut).
        local popThreshold = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.char_count * 5, 0.0, 0.95)
        local appeared = popInProgress >= popThreshold

        local vanishRank = math.floor(mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.char_count * 7, 0.0, 0.999)
            * ctx.char_count) + 1
        local picked = vanishProgress > 0.0 and vanishRank > visibleCount
        local aboutToBePicked = not picked and vanishProgress > 0.0 and vanishRank > nextVanishCount

        local fruitIndex = ((index + cutIndex) % #kFruits) + 1
        local fruitColor = kFruits[fruitIndex]

        local scaleSnap = mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt + 2, -kScaleSnapAmount, kScaleSnapAmount)
        local pickPop = aboutToBePicked and kPrePickScale or 1.0

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt, -kJitterAmount, kJitterAmount)
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt + 1, -kJitterAmount, kJitterAmount)
        character.scale = (1.0 + scaleSnap) * pickPop
        character.rotation =
            mt.random_range(seed, poseSalt + 4, -kRotationSnapDegrees, kRotationSnapDegrees)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = fruitColor
        character.shadow.use = true
        character.shadow.color = mt.color.with_alpha(fruitColor, 0.35)
        character.opacity = (appeared and not picked) and 1.0 or 0.0
    end
end
description: Showcase: fruit jump-cut telop. Sibling of 28_mono_cut.lua: the exact same quantized-cut grammar (no easing, one deterministic pose per cut), but the palette swaps from black-and-white to juicy fruit colors -- lemon, strawberry, lime, orange, grape, blueberry -- cycling one fruit forward on every cut, over a thick white candy stroke and a soft same-hue shadow. Intro: characters pop in over the first few cuts in random order. Outro: they are picked off one cut at a time, with a little scale pop on the cut before each one disappears.

name: 30_glitch.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: digital glitch telop. Parts corrupt in quantized cuts:
-- horizontal tears (strong X snap, slight Y), random stretch, a neon
-- fill flash with a contrasting stroke, and occasional one-cut dropouts.
-- The glitch density shapes the whole telop -- the intro materializes
-- the text OUT of a dense glitch storm (parts flicker as corruption
-- before they permanently exist), the hold keeps corruption rare, and
-- the outro ramps the storm back up until the signal cuts to nothing.
-- A rare whole-frame horizontal jump (sync loss) rides on top.
--
-- Everything is derived from quantized time + instance_seed, so each
-- frame is a deterministic pose and different instances glitch
-- differently.

local kGlitchFrequency = 12.0 -- cuts per second
local kIntroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds of the materializing storm
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds of the closing storm
local kSignalCutLead = 0.12 -- seconds of dead signal at the very end
local kHoldGlitchChance = 0.06 -- per-part corruption chance per cut while holding
local kStormGlitchChance = 0.75 -- corruption chance at full storm
local kDropoutChance = 0.05 -- per-part one-cut dropout chance while holding
local kTearOffsetX = 0.035 -- canvas fraction of the horizontal tear
local kTearOffsetY = 0.007 -- slight vertical component
local kTearStretchMin = 0.7 -- horizontal stretch range while corrupted
local kTearStretchMax = 1.6
local kSyncLossChance = 0.06 -- whole-frame jump chance per cut
local kSyncLossOffset = 0.02 -- canvas fraction of the frame jump
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Sync loss: the entire frame jumps sideways for single cuts.
    local cut = math.floor(ctx.time * kGlitchFrequency)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    ctx.global.position_x = 0.5
    if mt.random_range(seed + cut, 1, 0.0, 1.0) < kSyncLossChance then
        ctx.global.position_x = 0.5
            + mt.random_range(seed + cut, 2, -kSyncLossOffset, kSyncLossOffset)
    end
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local cut = math.floor(ctx.time * kGlitchFrequency)

    -- Storm strength: high while materializing, rare during the hold,
    -- ramping back up before the signal dies.
    local introStorm = 1.0 - mt.saturate(ctx.time / kIntroDuration)
    local outroStorm = mt.saturate(1.0 - (remainingSeconds - kSignalCutLead) / kOutroDuration)
    local storm = math.max(introStorm, outroStorm)
    local glitchChance = kHoldGlitchChance + (kStormGlitchChance - kHoldGlitchChance) * storm
    local signalAlive = remainingSeconds > kSignalCutLead

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]

        -- Materialize: each part permanently exists once the intro storm
        -- has decayed past its personal threshold; before that it only
        -- shows up as corruption flashes.
        local materializeThreshold = mt.random_range(seed, index + ctx.part_count * 5, 0.0, 0.9)
        local materialized = (1.0 - introStorm) >= materializeThreshold

        local corruptRoll = mt.random_range(seed + cut, index, 0.0, 1.0)
        local corrupted = corruptRoll < glitchChance
        local droppedOut = not corrupted
            and mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count, 0.0, 1.0) < kDropoutChance

        if corrupted then
            part.offset_x = 0.5
                + mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 2, -kTearOffsetX, kTearOffsetX)
            part.offset_y = 0.5
                + mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 3, -kTearOffsetY, kTearOffsetY)
            part.stretch_x =
                mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 4, kTearStretchMin, kTearStretchMax)
            -- Neon flash with a clashing stroke: a cheap chromatic split.
            local flashHue = mt.random_range(seed + cut, index + ctx.part_count * 6, 0.0, 1.0)
            part.fill.use = true
            part.fill.color = mt.color.from_hsv(flashHue, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
            part.stroke.use = true
            part.stroke.width = 0.005
            part.stroke.gap = 0.0
            part.stroke.color = mt.color.from_hsv(mt.wrap(flashHue + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0), 1.0, 1.0, 0.9)
        else
            part.offset_x = 0.5
            part.offset_y = 0.5
            part.stretch_x = 1.0
            part.fill.use = false
            part.stroke.use = false
        end

        local visible = corrupted or (materialized and not droppedOut)
        part.opacity = (signalAlive and visible) and 1.0 or 0.0
    end
end
description: Showcase: digital glitch telop. Parts corrupt in quantized cuts: horizontal tears (strong X snap, slight Y), random stretch, a neon fill flash with a contrasting stroke, and occasional one-cut dropouts. The glitch density shapes the whole telop -- the intro materializes the text OUT of a dense glitch storm (parts flicker as corruption before they permanently exist), the hold keeps corruption rare, and the outro ramps the storm back up until the signal cuts to nothing. A rare whole-frame horizontal jump (sync loss) rides on top.

name: 31_brake_pileup.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 2.8
-- Showcase: Brake Pileup (Comical, Physical & Animated Version) — the whole line sprints in from off-screen right,
-- the lead character slams on the brakes at its natural spot and pitches
-- forward from the sudden stop, and each trailing character keeps running
-- until it rams the pile, squashing slightly taller on impact. After a short
-- beat the line relaxes back to its natural spacing and proportions with elasticity.
--
-- Modified to be more comical: trailing impacts propagate forward, pushing and
-- squashing preceding characters further, and the recovery springs back elastically.
-- Characters now strictly respect physical boundaries and cannot slip past each other.
-- Running phase features an energetic cartoon-like bounce, a late deceleration (local brake)
-- right before impact so trailing characters run unaware until the collision, and a squash/stretch cycle.
-- Impact features a soft sub-frame cushion and phase-rounded ground landing.
-- Lean angle is held during the crash pile-up and recovers in sync with layout realignment.

local kEntryDistance = 1.1 -- canvas widths traveled before the brake point
local kBrakeTime = 0.7 -- seconds until the lead character halts in place
local kRunLean = -10.0 -- degrees; negative tips the glyph toward screen left (travel direction)
local kRunStretch = 0.15 -- extra horizontal stretch while sprinting
local kBrakeTip = -28.0 -- lead character's forward pitch at the brake moment
local kGapCompression = 0.45 -- compression factor of the piled spacing
local kPileTall = 0.18 -- baseline vertical squash stretch when piled up
local kImpactPunch = 0.08 -- impact stretch factor (subtle/restrained)
local kImpactFrequency = 3.5 -- lower frequency for the initial impact wiggle
local kImpactDamping = 10.0 -- high damping for the initial impact
local kHoldTime = 0.3 -- pause between the last crash and the realignment
local kRecoverDuration = 1.1 -- seconds to ease back into natural layout (longer for elastic settle)

-- Running animation parameters
local kRunFrequency = 16.0 -- step frequency (steps per second)
local kRunJumpHeight = 0.035 -- vertical bounce height
local kRunAngleOsc = 4.0 -- tilt oscillation amplitude while running
local kRunStretchOsc = 0.06 -- stretch oscillation amplitude while running

-- Cushion parameters (preventing single-frame harsh stops)
local kImpactRiseTime = 0.07 -- seconds taken to reach peak squish (soft cushion)
local kTipRiseTime = 0.05 -- seconds taken to reach peak forward lean (preventing 1-frame rotation snap)
local kOvertakeBuffer = 0.07 -- timeline buffer to blend the brake transition
local kLandDecay = 12.0 -- exponential decay rate for soft vertical landing (preventing drop snap)
local kDecelDuration = 0.18 -- seconds of late deceleration right before hitting the pile

local kRunSpeed = kEntryDistance / kBrakeTime -- canvas widths per second

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local leadX = ctx.chars[1].geometry.bounds_center_x

    -- Calculate crash times based on kinematics. Trailing characters have a longer distance
    -- to travel to the pile-up point, so they crash sequentially from front to back.
    local crashTimes = {}
    local pileShifts = {}
    local maxShift = 0.0
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local pileShift = (ctx.chars[index].geometry.bounds_center_x - leadX) * kGapCompression
        pileShifts[index] = pileShift
        crashTimes[index] = kBrakeTime + pileShift / kRunSpeed
        if pileShift > maxShift then
            maxShift = pileShift
        end
    end

    local lastCrashTime = kBrakeTime + maxShift / kRunSpeed
    local recoverStart = lastCrashTime + kHoldTime
    
    -- Elastic recovery easing
    local recover = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(
        mt.inverse_lerp(recoverStart, recoverStart + kRecoverDuration, ctx.time)
    ))

    -- Pass 1: Calculate temporary stretch, rotation, and offset_x / offset_y per character
    local stretchXs = {}
    local stretchYs = {}
    local rotations = {}
    local tempOffsetsX = {}
    local tempOffsetsY = {}

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local crashTime = crashTimes[index]
        local pileShift = pileShifts[index]

        local offsetX
        local offsetY
        local rotation
        local stretchX
        local stretchY

        -- Round total run cycle to the nearest integer multiple of pi so that
        -- the character always lands exactly on the ground (offsetY = 0.5) at the moment of impact.
        local rawSteps = crashTime * (kRunFrequency / math.pi)
        local roundedSteps = math.floor(rawSteps + 0.5)
        local targetRunCycle = roundedSteps * math.pi
        local brakeTimeStart = crashTime - kDecelDuration

        if ctx.time < crashTime then
            -- Sprint phase: sprint at constant speed initially, and apply a late deceleration
            -- (local brake) only when close to the crash point.
            local cycle
            local runStretch = kRunStretch
            
            if ctx.time < brakeTimeStart then
                -- Constant velocity sprint: unaware of the collision ahead
                offsetX = 0.5 + kEntryDistance - kRunSpeed * ctx.time
                cycle = ctx.time * kRunFrequency
                rotation = kRunLean + math.cos(cycle * 2.0) * kRunAngleOsc
                runStretch = kRunStretch + math.sin(cycle * 2.0) * kRunStretchOsc
            else
                -- Late deceleration phase: apply local ease-out quadratic brake to match speed profile
                local u = (ctx.time - brakeTimeStart) / kDecelDuration
                local ease = u * (2.0 - u) -- Out quadratic ease
                
                local xBrake = 0.5 + kEntryDistance - kRunSpeed * brakeTimeStart
                local xTarget = 0.5 - pileShift
                offsetX = mt.lerp(xBrake, xTarget, ease)
                
                -- Decelerate the foot stride cycle as well, aligning with ground phase-rounded end
                local cycleBrakeStart = brakeTimeStart * kRunFrequency
                cycle = mt.lerp(cycleBrakeStart, targetRunCycle, ease)
                
                -- Blend lean angle and stretch down to impact configuration
                rotation = mt.lerp(kRunLean + math.cos(cycle * 2.0) * kRunAngleOsc, kRunLean, ease)
                runStretch = mt.lerp(kRunStretch + math.sin(cycle * 2.0) * kRunStretchOsc, kRunStretch, ease)
            end
            
            offsetY = 0.5 + math.abs(math.sin(cycle)) * kRunJumpHeight
            stretchX = 1.0 + runStretch
            stretchY = 1.0 / (1.0 + runStretch)
        else
            -- Piled phase
            local sinceCrash = ctx.time - crashTime
            offsetX = 0.5 - pileShift
            
            -- Smoothly decay the last running jump bounce height to ground (0.5).
            local lastBounce = math.abs(math.sin(targetRunCycle)) * kRunJumpHeight
            offsetY = 0.5 + lastBounce * math.exp(-sinceCrash * kLandDecay)
            
            -- Hold the forward lean angle during the pile-up phase,
            -- and let it recover dynamically in sync with the physical layout recovery (recover).
            local rise = mt.saturate(sinceCrash / kTipRiseTime)
            local tipAngle = (index == 1) and kBrakeTip or kRunLean
            local baseRotation = tipAngle * rise
            
            -- Cushion the vertical stretch so the squash builds up over a few frames (kImpactRiseTime)
            local impactFactor = (sinceCrash / kImpactRiseTime) * math.exp(1.0 - sinceCrash / kImpactRiseTime)
            local punch = kImpactPunch * impactFactor
            local baseTall = kPileTall * mt.saturate(sinceCrash / kOvertakeBuffer) + punch

            -- Cascading impacts: trailing impacts propagate non-oscillating squeezing force forward
            local extraTall = 0.0
            local extraOffset = 0.0
            local extraRotation = 0.0

            for j = index + 1, ctx.char_count do
                local sinceOtherCrash = ctx.time - crashTimes[j]
                if sinceOtherCrash >= 0 then
                    local dist = j - index
                    local attenuation = 1.0 / (dist * 0.8 + 0.2) -- Attenuate the shock based on distance
                    
                    -- Smooth rise-and-decay impulse envelope for the shock wave
                    local press = (sinceOtherCrash / kImpactRiseTime) * math.exp(1.0 - sinceOtherCrash / kImpactRiseTime)

                    -- Additional vertical squashing is applied to all characters, including the lead
                    extraTall = extraTall + 0.08 * press * attenuation
                    
                    -- The lead character (index == 1) is the heaviest and remains anchored in position/angle
                    if index > 1 then
                        -- Shoved further left (forward)
                        extraOffset = extraOffset - 0.025 * press * attenuation
                        -- Tilted further forward from the shove
                        extraRotation = extraRotation - 6.0 * press * attenuation
                    end
                end
            end

            offsetX = offsetX + extraOffset
            rotation = baseRotation + extraRotation
            
            local tall = baseTall + extraTall
            stretchY = 1.0 + tall
            stretchX = 1.0 / (1.0 + tall)
        end

        stretchXs[index] = stretchX
        stretchYs[index] = stretchY
        rotations[index] = rotation
        tempOffsetsX[index] = offsetX
        tempOffsetsY[index] = offsetY
    end

    -- Pass 2: Boundary clamping with sub-frame cushion to prevent characters from slipping past each other
    local actualXs = {}
    local kOverlapFactor = 0.85 -- Allow slight overlapping for a squashed/packed visual feel

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local geom = character.geometry
        -- Temporary X position by adding offset to natural position
        local tempX = geom.bounds_center_x + (tempOffsetsX[index] - 0.5)

        if index == 1 then
            actualXs[1] = tempX
        else
            local prevGeom = ctx.chars[index - 1].geometry
            -- Consider current physical width scaled by stretch_x
            local curWidth = geom.bounds_width * stretchXs[index]
            local prevWidth = prevGeom.bounds_width * stretchXs[index - 1]
            
            -- Soften physical boundary on impact: momentarily allow a deeper overlap (cushion),
            -- then spring back to the default packed distance (kOverlapFactor).
            local currentOverlap = kOverlapFactor
            local sinceCrash = ctx.time - crashTimes[index]
            if sinceCrash >= 0 then
                local dip = 0.12 * math.exp(-sinceCrash * 6.0) -- Rapidly returns to normal packed state
                currentOverlap = kOverlapFactor - dip
            end
            
            -- Minimum distance for adjacent characters to touch
            local minDist = (curWidth + prevWidth) * 0.5 * currentOverlap
            
            -- Cannot move left of the preceding character's right boundary (prevent overtaking)
            actualXs[index] = math.max(tempX, actualXs[index - 1] + minDist)
        end
    end

    -- Pass 3: Back-calculate offset_x and apply final state values
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        
        -- Back-calculate the clamped offset_x in the piled state
        local clampedOffsetX = actualXs[index] - character.geometry.bounds_center_x + 0.5
        
        -- Blend with recovery easing and apply final transform values
        character.offset_x = mt.lerp(clampedOffsetX, 0.5, recover)
        character.offset_y = mt.lerp(tempOffsetsY[index], 0.5, recover)
        character.rotation = mt.lerp(rotations[index], 0.0, recover)
        character.stretch_x = mt.lerp(stretchXs[index], 1.0, recover)
        character.stretch_y = mt.lerp(stretchYs[index], 1.0, recover)
    end
end
description: Showcase: Brake Pileup (Comical, Physical & Animated Version) — the whole line sprints in from off-screen right, the lead character slams on the brakes at its natural spot and pitches forward from the sudden stop, and each trailing character keeps running until it rams the pile, squashing slightly taller on impact. After a short beat the line relaxes back to its natural spacing and proportions with elasticity.

name: 32_green_light.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- Showcase: green-light departure -- the exit counterpart to
-- 31_brake_pileup.lua, using the same cartoon running grammar in
-- reverse. The line waits at the start line, jogging in place with an
-- impatient rev; just before the light turns green every character
-- drops into a crouch at once; then they launch one by one from the
-- lead, each with a kick-off stretch, accelerating off screen left with
-- the full run-cycle bounce. The launch schedule is anchored to the
-- clip end so the last character always clears the frame in time.

local kReactionWindow = 0.9 -- seconds between the first and last launch
local kExitDuration = 1.1 -- seconds a character needs to clear the frame
local kCrouchLead = 0.25 -- seconds before the first launch the crouch hits
local kFallbackClipLength = 4.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kRevFrequency = 10.0 -- in-place jog steps per second while waiting
local kRevBounce = 0.008 -- canvas fraction of the waiting bounce
local kRevLean = -3.0 -- slight eager lean while waiting (negative = travel direction)
local kCrouchSquash = 0.18 -- vertical squash at the ready crouch
local kCrouchLean = 6.0 -- backward wind-up lean at the crouch
local kKickStretch = 0.3 -- horizontal stretch at the kick-off
local kRunLean = -12.0 -- forward lean while sprinting away
local kRunFrequency = 16.0 -- run-cycle steps per second
local kRunJumpHeight = 0.03 -- canvas fraction of the run bounce
local kAcceleration = 1.6 -- canvas widths per second^2 after launch

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local launchSpacing = kReactionWindow / characterCount

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]

        -- Remaining time at which this character launches: the lead
        -- (index 1) goes first, and the last launch still leaves
        -- kExitDuration to clear the frame.
        local launchRemaining = kExitDuration + kReactionWindow - (index - 1) * launchSpacing
        local sinceLaunch = launchRemaining - remainingSeconds
        local crouch = mt.saturate((sinceLaunch + kCrouchLead) / 0.1)

        local offsetX = 0.5
        local offsetY = 0.5
        local rotation
        local stretchX
        local stretchY

        if sinceLaunch >= 0.0 then
            -- Sprinting away: constant acceleration plus the run cycle.
            local kick = mt.saturate(sinceLaunch / 0.15)
            local cycle = sinceLaunch * kRunFrequency
            offsetX = 0.5 - 0.5 * kAcceleration * sinceLaunch * sinceLaunch
            offsetY = 0.5 + math.abs(math.sin(cycle)) * kRunJumpHeight * kick
            rotation = mt.lerp(kCrouchLean, kRunLean, kick)
            stretchX = 1.0 + kKickStretch * kick
            stretchY = 1.0 / (1.0 + kKickStretch * kick)
        elseif crouch > 0.0 then
            -- Ready crouch: everyone winds up together just before green.
            rotation = kCrouchLean * crouch
            stretchX = 1.0 + kCrouchSquash * crouch
            stretchY = 1.0 - kCrouchSquash * crouch
        else
            -- Impatient rev: jogging in place, phase-shifted per character.
            local revCycle = ctx.time * kRevFrequency + index * 1.7
            offsetY = 0.5 + math.abs(math.sin(revCycle)) * kRevBounce
            rotation = kRevLean + math.cos(revCycle * 2.0) * 1.5
            stretchX = 1.0 + math.sin(revCycle) * 0.02
            stretchY = 1.0 / stretchX
        end

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.offset_x = offsetX
        character.offset_y = offsetY
        character.rotation = rotation
        character.stretch_x = stretchX
        character.stretch_y = stretchY
    end
end

The launch schedule is anchored to the clip end so the last character always clears the frame in time.

name: 33_domino_shove.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4
-- Showcase: domino shove -- a variant of 31_brake_pileup.lua that turns
-- the impact propagation into ROTATION instead of compression. The line
-- is already standing when the last character arrives late, sprinting in
-- from the right at full speed (no brake -- it never saw the pile), and
-- rams the tail. A topple wave runs forward through the line: each
-- character pitches toward the front with distance-decayed strength and
-- springs back upright with an elastic wobble. The runner itself squashes
-- flat on impact and pops back. The outro is a staggered fade after the
-- line has recovered its composure.

local kImpactTime = 0.9 -- seconds until the runner hits the tail
local kEntryDistance = 1.0 -- canvas widths the runner travels
local kRunLean = -14.0 -- runner's forward lean while sprinting
local kRunFrequency = 16.0 -- run-cycle steps per second
local kRunJumpHeight = 0.03 -- canvas fraction of the run bounce
local kRunStretch = 0.18 -- speed stretch while sprinting
local kCrashSquash = 0.45 -- runner's horizontal squash at impact
local kCrashRecover = 0.8 -- seconds the runner takes to pop back
local kWaveDelay = 0.06 -- seconds the topple wave takes per character
local kTipMax = 26.0 -- degrees of forward pitch right next to the impact
local kTipRise = 0.07 -- seconds each tip takes to reach its peak
local kTipRecover = 0.9 -- seconds each character takes to spring upright
local kShoveDistance = 0.02 -- canvas fraction shoved forward at full strength
local kFadeLead = 0.6 -- seconds before clip end the fade starts
local kFadeStagger = 0.4 -- fade cascade across characters
local kFallbackClipLength = 4.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < 2 then
        return
    end

    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local fadeAmount = mt.saturate(1.0 - remainingSeconds / kFadeLead)
    local runnerIndex = ctx.char_count
    local runSpeed = kEntryDistance / kImpactTime

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]

        local offsetX = 0.5
        local offsetY = 0.5
        local rotation = 0.0
        local stretchX = 1.0
        local stretchY = 1.0

        if index == runnerIndex then
            if ctx.time < kImpactTime then
                -- Full-speed entry, blissfully unaware of the line ahead.
                local cycle = ctx.time * kRunFrequency
                offsetX = 0.5 + kEntryDistance - runSpeed * ctx.time
                offsetY = 0.5 + math.abs(math.sin(cycle)) * kRunJumpHeight
                rotation = kRunLean + math.cos(cycle * 2.0) * 4.0
                stretchX = 1.0 + kRunStretch
                stretchY = 1.0 / (1.0 + kRunStretch)
            else
                -- Face-first squash, then an elastic pop back to shape.
                local sinceCrash = ctx.time - kImpactTime
                local recover = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(sinceCrash / kCrashRecover))
                local squash = kCrashSquash * (1.0 - recover)
                rotation = kRunLean * (1.0 - recover)
                stretchX = 1.0 - squash
                stretchY = 1.0 + squash
            end
        else
            -- Topple wave: the shock reaches this character after a
            -- per-step delay and decays with the distance from the tail.
            local distanceFromImpact = runnerIndex - index
            local tipStart = kImpactTime + distanceFromImpact * kWaveDelay
            local sinceTip = ctx.time - tipStart
            if sinceTip >= 0.0 then
                local attenuation = 1.0 / (distanceFromImpact * 0.45 + 0.55)
                local rise = mt.saturate(sinceTip / kTipRise)
                local recover = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(sinceTip / kTipRecover))
                local strength = rise * (1.0 - recover) * attenuation

                rotation = -kTipMax * strength
                offsetX = 0.5 - kShoveDistance * strength
            end
        end

        local fadeStagger = mt.distribute(index, ctx.char_count) * kFadeStagger
        local fade = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(fadeAmount * (1.0 + fadeStagger) - fadeStagger))

        character.pivot_y = 0.5 - character.geometry.bounds_height * 0.5
        character.offset_x = offsetX
        character.offset_y = offsetY
        character.rotation = rotation
        character.stretch_x = stretchX
        character.stretch_y = stretchY
        character.opacity = 1.0 - fade
    end
end

The line is already standing when the last character arrives late, sprinting in from the right at full speed (no brake -- it never saw the pile), and rams the tail. A topple wave runs forward through the line: each character pitches toward the front with distance-decayed strength and springs back upright with an elastic wobble. The runner itself squashes flat on impact and pops back. The outro is a staggered fade after the line has recovered its composure.

name: 34_light_sweep_prism.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: Light Sweep Prism — a tilted band of light sweeps across the
-- text; as it touches each part, the part lifts toward the camera,
-- flashes white, then settles into a spectral color derived from its
-- position, as if the light refracted through the glyphs.
--
-- Spatial field animation: the driver is each part's signed distance to
-- the moving band line, computed from part.geometry.canvas_center_x/y in
-- aspect-corrected world space — parts respond by where they physically
-- are, not by index, so the light visibly travels *through* characters
-- rather than jumping glyph to glyph.
--
-- The sweep ping-pongs, revealing on the way out and un-revealing on the
-- way back, so the loop has no visible reset. The lift uses part.z and
-- reads best under the 3D preset; the accompanying scale bump keeps the
-- flash legible in 2D as well.

local kSweepPeriod = 5.0 -- seconds for one full out-and-back sweep
local kSweepAngle = math.rad(20.0) -- tilt of the sweep direction from horizontal
local kBandWidth = 0.09 -- gaussian half-width of the light band, world units
local kSweepReach = 0.9 -- world-space distance the band travels past center
local kLiftHeight = 0.25 -- part.z at full flash
local kBaseHue = 0.55 -- resting hue the prism colors are spread around

local function gaussian(distance, width)
    return math.exp(-(distance * distance) / (width * width))
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local aspect = ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio
    local sweepX = math.cos(kSweepAngle)
    local sweepY = math.sin(kSweepAngle)
    local bandPosition = mt.lerp(-kSweepReach, kSweepReach, mt.pingpong(ctx.time, kSweepPeriod))

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local geometry = part.geometry
        local worldX = (geometry.canvas_center_x - 0.5) * aspect
        local worldY = geometry.canvas_center_y - 0.5

        -- Signed distance along the sweep direction: negative once the
        -- band has passed this part.
        local signedDistance = (worldX * sweepX + worldY * sweepY) - bandPosition

        local flash = gaussian(signedDistance, kBandWidth)
        local lit = mt.smoothstep(0.0, 0.1, -signedDistance)

        -- Spectral color: hue fans out with position so neighboring
        -- parts refract into neighboring wavelengths.
        local prismHue = mt.wrap(kBaseHue + worldY * 0.35 + worldX * 0.12, 0.0, 1.0)
        local prismColor = mt.color.from_hsv(prismHue, 0.65, 1.0, 1.0)
        local dimColor = { r = 0.32, g = 0.33, b = 0.38, a = 1.0 }
        local white = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }

        local settled = mt.color.lerp(dimColor, prismColor, lit)

        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(settled, white, flash)
        part.z = flash * kLiftHeight
        part.scale = 1.0 + flash * 0.15
    end
end

name: 35_focus_flow.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- Showcase: focus-sweep telop. The line itself never moves -- it sits
-- wherever the telop is placed. Instead a magnifying focus RUNS THROUGH
-- it, briskly, exactly twice: the intro sweep reveals each character
-- with a pop as it crosses (characters ahead of it do not exist yet),
-- and the outro sweep wipes them away again behind it. Between sweeps
-- the line holds still as a plain readable telop with only a micro
-- rotation drift.
--
-- While the focus crosses a character, that character swells (out_back
-- gives it a small pop past its peak) and mt.layout.reflow reflows
-- the neighbors around it -- anchored on the focused character at its
-- own natural spot with baseline = "natural", so the swell pushes
-- neighbors aside horizontally while the line's position and height
-- stay rock solid.
--
-- Both sweeps run at a fixed real-time rate per character (compressed
-- only when the clip is too short for two full passes).

local kSecondsPerCharacter = 0.09 -- sweep rate; smaller = snappier
local kSweepPadding = 1.5 -- the sweep starts/ends this many characters off each end
local kMaxSweepClipFraction = 0.4 -- one sweep may occupy at most this clip fraction
local kFocusBoost = 0.45 -- extra scale at the focus center
local kFocusSigma = 1.4 -- gaussian width of the focus, in characters
local kRetypesetTracking = 0.012 -- spacing handed to mt.layout.reflow
local kRevealSoftness = 1.2 -- how tightly appearance hugs the passing focus
local kWiggleDegrees = 1.1 -- micro rotation drift keeping the hold organic
local kWiggleSpeed = 0.8 -- wiggle time scale
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kRestFill = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 } -- resting color of the line
local kFocusFill = { r = 1.0, g = 0.78, b = 0.25, a = 1.0 } -- accent while the focus crosses

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local remainingSeconds = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx, kFallbackClipLength)
    local clipLength = kFallbackClipLength
    if ctx.timeline.available then
        clipLength = ctx.timeline.duration_seconds
    end
    local characterCount = ctx.char_count

    -- Sweep pacing: fixed real seconds per character, compressed only
    -- when two sweeps would not fit in the clip.
    local sweepSpan = characterCount + 2.0 * kSweepPadding
    local secondsPerCharacter =
        math.min(kSecondsPerCharacter, clipLength * kMaxSweepClipFraction / sweepSpan)
    local sweepDuration = sweepSpan * secondsPerCharacter

    -- Focus positions in index space. The intro sweep starts at clip
    -- start; the outro sweep ends exactly at clip end.
    local introFocus = -kSweepPadding + ctx.time / secondsPerCharacter
    local outroFocus = -kSweepPadding + (sweepDuration - remainingSeconds) / secondsPerCharacter

    -- Pass 1: swell, reveal, and wipe. Scale must be final before the
    -- reflow so retypeset sees the true character widths.
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local introDistance = index - introFocus
        local outroDistance = index - outroFocus
        local focus = math.max(
            math.exp(-(introDistance * introDistance) / (kFocusSigma * kFocusSigma)),
            math.exp(-(outroDistance * outroDistance) / (kFocusSigma * kFocusSigma)))

        -- A character exists from the moment the intro focus reaches it
        -- until the outro focus has passed over it.
        local revealed = mt.smoothstep(-kRevealSoftness, 0.0, introFocus - index)
        local wiped = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kRevealSoftness, outroFocus - index)

        character.scale = 1.0 + kFocusBoost * mt.ease.out_quad(focus)
        character.opacity = revealed * (1.0 - wiped)
        character.rotation = mt.wiggle(ctx.time * kWiggleSpeed, 2.5, kWiggleDegrees, 2, index * 10)

        -- Color rides the same focus weight as the swell, so the accent
        -- travels with the magnifier and cools back to the resting color.
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(kRestFill, kFocusFill, focus)
    end

    -- Pass 2: reflow around the line's center character. Using a stable
    -- center anchor prevents discrete jumps when focus shifts across indices.
    local anchorIndex = math.ceil(ctx.char_count / 2)
    ctx.chars[anchorIndex].offset_x = 0.5
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, kRetypesetTracking, {
        mode = "horizontal",
        anchor = anchorIndex,
    })
end
description: Showcase: focus-sweep telop. The line itself never moves -- it sits wherever the telop is placed. Instead a magnifying focus RUNS THROUGH it, briskly, exactly twice: the intro sweep reveals each character with a pop as it crosses (characters ahead of it do not exist yet), and the outro sweep wipes them away again behind it. Between sweeps the line holds still as a plain readable telop with only a micro rotation drift.

name: 36_hiccup.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- Showcase: hiccup telop. The line is a perfectly still, readable telop
-- almost all of the time -- but every couple of seconds one random
-- character suddenly puffs up and elastically settles back, and the
-- partial retypeset squeezes its neighbors aside for that moment (the
-- accordion trick from mt.layout.reflow with an anchor). The layout
-- is only touched while a hiccup is actually in flight, so the resting
-- telop keeps its exact host layout, kerning and all.
--
-- Hiccup times and positions come from closed-form instance_seed
-- randomness, so scrubbing is deterministic and every instance hiccups
-- on its own schedule.

local kIntroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kFadeStagger = 0.3 -- entrance/exit cascade across characters
local kFirstHiccupDelay = 1.2 -- seconds before the first hiccup
local kHiccupInterval = 1.7 -- average seconds between hiccups
local kHiccupJitter = 0.8 -- random extra delay per hiccup
local kSwellAmount = 0.45 -- extra scale at the peak of a hiccup
local kSwellRise = 0.09 -- seconds the puff takes to reach its peak
local kSettleDuration = 0.7 -- seconds the elastic settle takes
local kMaxEvents = 64 -- scheduling scan limit
local kFallbackClipLength = 8.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

    -- Find the most recent hiccup at or before now. Events are spaced by
    -- at least the base interval, so at most one is ever in flight.
    local latestOrdinal = 0
    local latestTime = 0.0
    local eventTime = kFirstHiccupDelay
    for ordinal = 1, kMaxEvents do
        eventTime = eventTime + mt.random_range(seed, ordinal, 0.0, kHiccupJitter)
        if eventTime > ctx.time then
            break
        end
        latestOrdinal = ordinal
        latestTime = eventTime
        eventTime = eventTime + kHiccupInterval
    end

    -- Hiccups only fire while the telop is fully on screen.
    local calm = mt.saturate(introAmount * 2.0 - 1.0) * (1.0 - outroAmount)
    local swell = 0.0
    local hiccupIndex = 1
    if latestOrdinal > 0 then
        local sinceHiccup = ctx.time - latestTime
        local rise = mt.saturate(sinceHiccup / kSwellRise)
        local settle = mt.ease.out_elastic(mt.saturate(sinceHiccup / kSettleDuration))
        swell = kSwellAmount * rise * (1.0 - settle) * calm
        hiccupIndex = math.floor(mt.random_range(
            seed, latestOrdinal + kMaxEvents, 1.0, ctx.char_count + 0.999))
        hiccupIndex = mt.clamp(hiccupIndex, 1, ctx.char_count)
    end

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, ctx.char_count) * kFadeStagger
        local appear = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local vanish = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        character.opacity = appear * (1.0 - vanish)
    end

    -- Touch the layout only while a hiccup is visibly in flight, so the
    -- resting telop keeps the untouched host layout.
    if swell > 0.001 then
        ctx.chars[hiccupIndex].scale = 1.0 + swell
        ctx.chars[hiccupIndex].offset_x = 0.5
        mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, {
            anchor = hiccupIndex,
        })
    end
end

The layout is only touched while a hiccup is actually in flight, so the resting telop keeps its exact host layout, kerning and all.

name: 37_pass_through.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- Showcase: something-runs-under-it telop. The line rests perfectly
-- still, but every few seconds an invisible little something scurries
-- along it: a local gap opens at the runner's position -- characters
-- lean apart and slide aside just around that point -- travels down the
-- line, and snaps shut behind it. The opening is a signed, distance-
-- decayed horizontal push (pure offset_x), so the ends of the line
-- barely move and nothing is ever distorted; direction alternates and
-- schedules are deterministic per instance.

local kIntroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kFadeStagger = 0.3 -- entrance/exit cascade across characters
local kFirstPassDelay = 1.3 -- seconds before the first run
local kPassInterval = 2.2 -- average seconds between runs
local kPassJitter = 0.9 -- random extra delay per run
local kPassDuration = 0.55 -- seconds one run takes end to end
local kGapWidth = 0.016 -- canvas fraction each side is pushed at the peak
local kGapSpread = 1.3 -- characters over which the push decays
local kTiltDegrees = 7.0 -- characters lean away from the runner
local kMaxEvents = 64 -- scheduling scan limit
local kFallbackClipLength = 8.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local characterCount = ctx.char_count

    -- Most recent run at or before now (never more than one in flight).
    local latestOrdinal = 0
    local latestTime = 0.0
    local eventTime = kFirstPassDelay
    for ordinal = 1, kMaxEvents do
        eventTime = eventTime + mt.random_range(seed, ordinal, 0.0, kPassJitter)
        if eventTime > ctx.time then
            break
        end
        latestOrdinal = ordinal
        latestTime = eventTime
        eventTime = eventTime + kPassInterval
    end

    local calm = mt.saturate(introAmount * 2.0 - 1.0) * (1.0 - outroAmount)
    local gapStrength = 0.0
    local runnerPosition = 0.0
    if latestOrdinal > 0 then
        local runProgress = (ctx.time - latestTime) / kPassDuration
        if runProgress <= 1.0 then
            -- The gap eases open on entry and shut on exit of the run.
            gapStrength = math.sin(mt.saturate(runProgress) * math.pi) * calm
            -- Runner travels past both ends; direction alternates.
            local span = characterCount + 2.0 * kGapSpread
            local along = -kGapSpread + runProgress * span
            if latestOrdinal % 2 == 0 then
                along = characterCount + kGapSpread - runProgress * span
            end
            runnerPosition = along
        end
    end

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, characterCount) * kFadeStagger
        local appear = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local vanish = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        character.opacity = appear * (1.0 - vanish)

        if gapStrength > 0.001 then
            local distance = index - runnerPosition
            local falloff = math.exp(-(distance * distance) / (kGapSpread * kGapSpread))
            local side = 1.0
            if distance < 0.0 then
                side = -1.0
            end
            character.offset_x = 0.5 + side * falloff * kGapWidth * gapStrength
            character.rotation = side * falloff * kTiltDegrees * gapStrength
        end
    end
end

The opening is a signed, distance- decayed horizontal push (pure offset_x), so the ends of the line barely move and nothing is ever distorted; direction alternates and schedules are deterministic per instance.

name: 38_word_pulse.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6
-- Showcase: a clearly readable emphasized-word heartbeat.
--
-- The displayed line is:
--
--     HERE|PULSE!|>
--          ^^^^^^
--
-- "PULSE!" beats as one coherent phrase. The left divider remains fixed,
-- while the right divider and arrow move aside as the phrase expands. This
-- makes mt.layout.reflow's partial-layout effect directly visible without
-- mixing it with per-character phase waves or unrelated motion.

local kWordStart = 6
local kWordEnd = 11
local kLeftDividerIndex = 5
local kRightDividerIndex = 12
local kIntroDuration = 0.45
local kOutroDuration = 0.55
local kFirstHeartbeatTime = 0.9
local kHeartbeatPeriod = 1.55
local kHeartbeatScale = 0.42
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kBaseFill = { r = 0.92, g = 0.95, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
local kDividerFill = { r = 0.25, g = 0.7, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
local kWordRestFill = { r = 1.0, g = 0.72, b = 0.18, a = 1.0 }
local kWordBeatFill = { r = 1.0, g = 0.18, b = 0.08, a = 1.0 }

local function pulseWindow(time, startTime, peakTime, endTime)
    local amount = 0.0
    if time >= startTime and time <= endTime then
        if time <= peakTime then
            amount = mt.smoothstep(startTime, peakTime, time)
        else
            amount = 1.0 - mt.smoothstep(peakTime, endTime, time)
        end
    end
    return amount
end

local function heartbeatAmount(time)
    local amount = 0.0
    if time >= kFirstHeartbeatTime then
        local beatTime = (time - kFirstHeartbeatTime) % kHeartbeatPeriod
        local primaryBeat = pulseWindow(beatTime, 0.0, 0.09, 0.3)
        local secondaryBeat = 0.52 * pulseWindow(beatTime, 0.31, 0.39, 0.62)
        amount = math.max(primaryBeat, secondaryBeat)
    end
    return amount
end

local function setPivotToHorizontalOrigin(character)
    local geometry = character.geometry
    character.pivot_x = 0.5 + geometry.canvas_origin_x - geometry.bounds_center_x
    character.pivot_y = 0.5 + geometry.canvas_origin_y - geometry.bounds_center_y
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.text = "HERE|PULSE!|>"
    ctx.global.vertical = false
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count < kRightDividerIndex then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(
            ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local visibility = mt.ease.out_quad(introAmount) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount))
    local heartbeat = heartbeatAmount(ctx.time) * visibility
    local emphasizedScale = 1.0 + kHeartbeatScale * heartbeat

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        character.opacity = visibility
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = kBaseFill

        if index == kLeftDividerIndex or index >= kRightDividerIndex then
            character.fill.color = kDividerFill
        end

        if index >= kWordStart and index <= kWordEnd then
            character.scale = emphasizedScale
            character.fill.color =
                mt.color.lerp(kWordRestFill, kWordBeatFill, heartbeat)

            -- Scaling around each glyph's horizontal typesetting origin
            -- keeps the word on a stable baseline.
            setPivotToHorizontalOrigin(character)
        end
    end

    -- Only the emphasized word and its suffix participate. The word's first
    -- character is the fixed anchor, so "HERE|" never moves. The right
    -- divider and arrow visibly absorb the word's changing advance.
    local reflowTargets = {}
    for index = kWordStart, ctx.char_count do
        table.insert(reflowTargets, index)
    end

    local anchor = ctx.chars[kWordStart]
    anchor.offset_x = 0.5
    anchor.offset_y = 0.5
    mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, {
        targets = reflowTargets,
        anchor = kWordStart,
        mode = "horizontal",
    })
end
description: Showcase: a clearly readable emphasized-word heartbeat.

name: 39_bellows_wave.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- Showcase: bellows-wave telop. The line rests still; every few seconds
-- a compression wave is born at a random character and races toward
-- both ends -- each character it crosses is first squeezed narrow, then
-- pulled wide, then released (a derivative-of-gaussian pulse on
-- stretch_x), with a cool tint riding the wavefront. The retypeset
-- anchored at the wave's origin turns those width changes into true
-- accordion spacing: pleats fold and unfold as the wave passes. Layout
-- is only touched while a wave is alive.

local kIntroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.6 -- seconds
local kFadeStagger = 0.3 -- entrance/exit cascade across characters
local kFirstWaveDelay = 1.2 -- seconds before the first wave
local kWaveInterval = 2.4 -- average seconds between waves
local kWaveJitter = 1.0 -- random extra delay per wave
local kWaveSpeed = 14.0 -- characters per second the front travels
local kPulseWidth = 1.1 -- characters wide the squeeze/stretch pulse is
local kPulseAmount = 0.3 -- stretch_x swing at the peak
local kTintStrength = 0.8 -- how strongly the tint rides the front
local kMaxEvents = 64 -- scheduling scan limit
local kFallbackClipLength = 8.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kBaseFill = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }
local kWaveFill = { r = 0.45, g = 0.75, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local characterCount = ctx.char_count

    -- Most recent wave at or before now.
    local latestOrdinal = 0
    local latestTime = 0.0
    local eventTime = kFirstWaveDelay
    for ordinal = 1, kMaxEvents do
        eventTime = eventTime + mt.random_range(seed, ordinal, 0.0, kWaveJitter)
        if eventTime > ctx.time then
            break
        end
        latestOrdinal = ordinal
        latestTime = eventTime
        eventTime = eventTime + kWaveInterval
    end

    local calm = mt.saturate(introAmount * 2.0 - 1.0) * (1.0 - outroAmount)
    local waveAlive = false
    local originIndex = 1
    local frontDistance = 0.0
    if latestOrdinal > 0 then
        originIndex = math.floor(mt.random_range(
            seed, latestOrdinal + kMaxEvents, 1.0, characterCount + 0.999))
        originIndex = mt.clamp(originIndex, 1, characterCount)
        frontDistance = (ctx.time - latestTime) * kWaveSpeed
        -- The wave dies once the front has cleared the farther end.
        local farthestReach = math.max(originIndex - 1, characterCount - originIndex)
            + kPulseWidth * 3.0
        waveAlive = frontDistance <= farthestReach and calm > 0.001
    end

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, characterCount) * kFadeStagger
        local appear = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local vanish = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        character.opacity = appear * (1.0 - vanish)

        if waveAlive then
            -- Signed distance from the wavefront: negative before the
            -- front arrives, positive after it has passed. The pulse
            -- squeezes just ahead of the front and stretches just
            -- behind it (derivative-of-gaussian profile).
            local behindFront = frontDistance - math.abs(index - originIndex)
            local normalized = behindFront / kPulseWidth
            local pulse = -normalized * math.exp(-normalized * normalized)

            character.stretch_x = 1.0 + pulse * kPulseAmount * 2.0 * calm
            local tint = math.exp(-normalized * normalized) * kTintStrength * calm
            character.fill.use = true
            character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(kBaseFill, kWaveFill, tint)
        end
    end

    -- Accordion spacing: reflow around the wave's origin so the width
    -- pulse folds real pleats instead of overlapping glyphs.
    if waveAlive then
        ctx.chars[originIndex].offset_x = 0.5
        mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, {
            anchor = originIndex,
        })
    end
end
description: Showcase: bellows-wave telop. The line rests still; every few seconds a compression wave is born at a random character and races toward both ends -- each character it crosses is first squeezed narrow, then pulled wide, then released (a derivative-of-gaussian pulse on stretch_x), with a cool tint riding the wavefront. The retypeset anchored at the wave's origin turns those width changes into true accordion spacing: pleats fold and unfold as the wave passes. Layout is only touched while a wave is alive.

name: 40_calm_breath.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- Showcase: calm breathing telop, built for text that stays on screen a
-- long time. The whole line inhales and exhales on a slow cycle --
-- a few percent of scale, with a soft brightness swell riding the same
-- breath -- and a slight per-character phase lag keeps it from feeling
-- mechanical. Amplitudes are tuned to be clearly alive at a glance
-- while staying easy to read past.
--
-- Everything is driven by ctx.time alone, so the loop is seamless at
-- any clip length; the intro and outro are plain quiet fades.

local kIntroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kBreathPeriod = 5.0 -- seconds per full breath
local kBreathScale = 0.03 -- scale amplitude of the breath
local kBreathBrightness = 0.1 -- opacity amplitude riding the breath
local kPhaseLag = 0.4 -- radians of per-character lag along the line
local kFallbackClipLength = 8.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(introAmount)
    local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local phase = index * kPhaseLag
        local breath = mt.wave(ctx.time, 1.0 / kBreathPeriod, phase)

        character.scale = 1.0 + breath * kBreathScale
        character.opacity = (1.0 - kBreathBrightness + breath * kBreathBrightness)
            * fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end
description: Showcase: calm breathing telop, built for text that stays on screen a long time. The whole line inhales and exhales on a slow cycle -- a few percent of scale, with a soft brightness swell riding the same breath -- and a slight per-character phase lag keeps it from feeling mechanical. Amplitudes are tuned to be clearly alive at a glance while staying easy to read past.

name: 41_water_float.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- Showcase: water-float telop for long-running on-screen text. Where
-- 40_calm_breath.lua moves the line as one organism, here every
-- character floats independently -- a very slow, deterministic noise
-- drift in position and a faint rotation sway, each character on its
-- own period and phase, like leaves resting on still water. Amplitudes
-- stay small enough that the text reads as static.
--
-- All motion is smooth noise over ctx.time (no events, no loop seam);
-- the intro and outro are plain quiet fades.

local kIntroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kDriftAmount = 0.01 -- canvas fraction of the positional drift
local kDriftSpeed = 0.28 -- noise time scale; smaller = slower water
local kSwayDegrees = 2.5 -- rotation amplitude
local kSwaySpeed = 0.22 -- rotation noise time scale
local kFallbackClipLength = 8.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(introAmount)
    local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        -- Per-character speed variance keeps neighbors from ever locking
        -- into step with each other.
        local speedScale = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.8, 1.25)

        character.offset_x = 0.5
            + mt.noise1(ctx.time * kDriftSpeed * speedScale + index * 3.1, 51) * kDriftAmount
        character.offset_y = 0.5
            + mt.noise1(ctx.time * kDriftSpeed * speedScale + index * 3.1, 52) * kDriftAmount
        character.rotation =
            mt.noise1(ctx.time * kSwaySpeed * speedScale + index * 5.7, 53) * kSwayDegrees
        character.opacity = fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end
description: Showcase: water-float telop for long-running on-screen text. Where 40_calm_breath.lua moves the line as one organism, here every character floats independently -- a very slow, deterministic noise drift in position and a faint rotation sway, each character on its own period and phase, like leaves resting on still water. Amplitudes stay small enough that the text reads as static.

name: 42_quiet_sheen.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 12
-- Showcase: quiet sheen telop for long-running on-screen text. The line
-- is completely still; every ten-plus seconds a soft band of light
-- drifts across it, lifting brightness by a few percent -- no color
-- change, no motion, just a slow glint like a light source moving
-- somewhere off screen. Between passes the telop is truly static.
--
-- The band is positional (each character's canvas x against a moving
-- front), so multi-line text catches the light as one surface. Driven
-- by ctx.time only; the intro and outro are plain quiet fades.

local kIntroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kSheenPeriod = 7.0 -- seconds between the starts of two passes
local kSheenTravelTime = 2.2 -- seconds one pass takes to cross the canvas
local kSheenHalfWidth = 0.16 -- canvas fraction, soft half-width of the band
local kSheenBrightness = 0.25 -- brightness lift at the band's center
local kBaseFill = { r = 0.78, g = 0.78, b = 0.8, a = 1.0 }
local kFallbackClipLength = 12.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.fill.color = kBaseFill
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(introAmount)
    local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount)

    -- Band front position: it crosses the canvas during the first
    -- kSheenTravelTime of each period, then rests far off screen.
    local cycleTime = ctx.time % kSheenPeriod
    local travel = mt.saturate(cycleTime / kSheenTravelTime)
    local front = -kSheenHalfWidth * 2.0
        + mt.ease.in_out_sine(travel) * (1.0 + 4.0 * kSheenHalfWidth)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local distance = character.geometry.bounds_center_x - front
        local glint = math.exp(-(distance * distance) / (kSheenHalfWidth * kSheenHalfWidth))

        local lift = glint * kSheenBrightness
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = {
            r = mt.clamp(kBaseFill.r + lift, 0.0, 1.0),
            g = mt.clamp(kBaseFill.g + lift, 0.0, 1.0),
            b = mt.clamp(kBaseFill.b + lift, 0.0, 1.0),
            a = 1.0,
        }
        character.opacity = fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end
description: Showcase: quiet sheen telop for long-running on-screen text. The line is completely still; every ten-plus seconds a soft band of light drifts across it, lifting brightness by a few percent -- no color change, no motion, just a slow glint like a light source moving somewhere off screen. Between passes the telop is truly static.

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 12
-- Showcase: sundial telop for long-running on-screen text. The text
-- itself never moves at all -- only its drop shadow lives: the shadow's
-- angle sweeps around like the sun crossing a sped-up sky (about twenty
-- seconds per revolution) while its distance eases in and out, so a viewer
-- who glances back at the telop later senses that time has passed
-- without ever being distracted by motion. A streamer's always-on
-- caption is the intended use.
--
-- Shadow parameters are base values, so the animation lives entirely in
-- OnPreLayout; OnLayout only handles the quiet fades.

local kIntroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.7 -- seconds
local kSunPeriod = 20.0 -- seconds per full revolution of the shadow angle
local kStartAngle = 300.0 -- degrees, where the "sun" starts
local kBaseDistance = 1.6 -- percent of the canvas short side (1.0 = 1%)
local kDistanceSwing = 0.8 -- slow in/out easing of the distance, same unit
local kDistancePeriod = 9.0 -- seconds per distance cycle (offset from kSunPeriod)
local kShadowColor = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0, a = 0.5 }
local kFallbackClipLength = 12.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = kStartAngle + ctx.time * (360.0 / kSunPeriod)
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = kBaseDistance
        + mt.wave(ctx.time, 1.0 / kDistancePeriod) * kDistanceSwing
    ctx.global.shadow.color = kShadowColor
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local fadeIn = mt.ease.out_quad(introAmount)
    local fadeOut = mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        ctx.chars[index].opacity = fadeIn * (1.0 - fadeOut)
    end
end
