name: 44_vertical_fall.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend lang ja pos 0.5 0.85 bg #1e1e1e
-- Showcase: vertical sudare telop. Classic Japanese vertical caption:
-- the text is set in columns (right column first) and the characters
-- drop softly into place in reading order -- top to bottom, column by
-- column -- like a bamboo blind being lowered one slat at a time. The
-- outro continues the motion: everything slips further down and fades.
--
-- Reading order in vertical text IS the character index order, so a
-- plain index stagger produces the top-to-bottom, right-to-left cascade
-- with no extra bookkeeping.

local kIntroDuration = 1.0 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.6 -- reading-order cascade across characters
local kDropDistance = 0.1 -- canvas fraction fallen during the intro
local kExitDistance = 0.08 -- canvas fraction slipped during the outro

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.text = "いろはにほへと\nちりぬるを"
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.15
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kStaggerAmount
        local settle = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local slip = mt.ease.in_cubic(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + (1.0 - settle) * kDropDistance - slip * kExitDistance
        character.opacity = settle * (1.0 - slip)
    end
end
description: Showcase: vertical sudare telop. Classic Japanese vertical caption: the text is set in columns (right column first) and the characters drop softly into place in reading order -- top to bottom, column by column -- like a bamboo blind being lowered one slat at a time. The outro continues the motion: everything slips further down and fades.

name: 45_vertical_unroll.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend lang ja pos 0.5 0.85 bg #1e1e1e
-- Showcase: hanging-scroll telop. The vertical text is revealed the way
-- a kakejiku unrolls: a soft front descends the canvas and characters
-- appear as it passes their height -- all columns together, since the
-- front is positional (bounds_center_y), not index-based. Characters
-- just below the front lag upward a touch, like paper still curled
-- around the roller. The outro rolls the scroll back up: a second front
-- rises from the bottom and hides characters beneath it.

local kIntroDuration = 1.1 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.9 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kEdgeSoftness = 0.07 -- canvas fraction over which the front feathers
local kCurlLag = 0.015 -- canvas fraction of the upward curl near the front

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.text = "春はあけぼの\nやうやうしろく"
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.15
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    -- Text extents in canvas space (Y-up), padded so the feathered
    -- fronts fully clear both ends.
    local topEdge = -math.huge
    local bottomEdge = math.huge
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local geometry = ctx.chars[index].geometry
        topEdge = math.max(topEdge, geometry.bounds_center_y + geometry.bounds_height * 0.5)
        bottomEdge = math.min(bottomEdge, geometry.bounds_center_y - geometry.bounds_height * 0.5)
    end
    topEdge = topEdge + kEdgeSoftness
    bottomEdge = bottomEdge - kEdgeSoftness

    -- Unroll front descends from the top; roll-up front climbs from the
    -- bottom (canvas Y grows upward, so descending means decreasing).
    local unrollFront = topEdge
        - mt.ease.in_out_sine(introAmount) * (topEdge - bottomEdge)
    local rollUpFront = bottomEdge
        + mt.ease.in_out_sine(outroAmount) * (topEdge - bottomEdge)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local positionY = character.geometry.bounds_center_y

        local revealed = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kEdgeSoftness, positionY - unrollFront)
        local hidden = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kEdgeSoftness, rollUpFront - positionY)
        if outroAmount <= 0.0 then
            hidden = 0.0
        end

        -- Paper curl: characters right at the front sit a touch high,
        -- easing down as the roller moves past them.
        local frontDistance = positionY - unrollFront
        local curl = math.exp(-(frontDistance * frontDistance)
            / (kEdgeSoftness * kEdgeSoftness)) * kCurlLag

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + curl * (1.0 - mt.saturate(introAmount * 2.0 - 1.0))
        character.opacity = revealed * (1.0 - hidden)
    end
end
description: Showcase: hanging-scroll telop. The vertical text is revealed the way a kakejiku unrolls: a soft front descends the canvas and characters appear as it passes their height -- all columns together, since the front is positional (bounds_center_y), not index-based. Characters just below the front lag upward a touch, like paper still curled around the roller. The outro rolls the scroll back up: a second front rises from the bottom and hides characters beneath it.

name: 46_vertical_sway.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 8
-- @recommend lang ja pos 0.5 0.85 bg #1e1e1e
-- Showcase: tanzaku telop. Each vertical column hangs like a paper strip
-- tied at its top: the whole strip swings gently in a slow breeze, and
-- the swing grows with hanging depth -- the top character barely moves
-- while the bottom one drifts the most, with a slight phase delay
-- traveling down the strip like a wave along the paper. Columns swing on
-- their own phases (line_index), so the strips never move in lockstep.
-- Quiet enough for long-running captions; intro and outro are fades.

local kIntroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 0.8 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 8.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kSwaySpeed = 0.22 -- swings per second
local kSwayDegrees = 3.0 -- character tilt at the deepest point
local kSwayDrift = 0.055 -- horizontal drift per unit of hanging depth
local kColumnPhase = 1.4 -- radians between neighboring columns
local kDepthLag = 2.6 -- radians of wave lag per unit of hanging depth
local kBreezeSpeed = 0.11 -- slow noise that varies the breeze strength
local kFadeStagger = 0.3 -- entrance/exit cascade across characters

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.text = "たなばたさま\nささのはさらさら"
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.2
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    if ctx.char_count == 0 then
        return
    end

    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    -- The tie point: the top edge of the laid-out text (canvas Y-up).
    local topEdge = -math.huge
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local geometry = ctx.chars[index].geometry
        topEdge = math.max(topEdge, geometry.bounds_center_y + geometry.bounds_height * 0.5)
    end

    -- The breeze swells and dies on smooth noise, shared by all strips.
    local breeze = 0.6 + 0.4 * mt.noise1(ctx.time * kBreezeSpeed, 61)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local depth = math.max(topEdge - character.geometry.bounds_center_y, 0.0)
        local phase = character.line_index * kColumnPhase - depth * kDepthLag
        local swing = mt.wave(ctx.time, kSwaySpeed, phase) * breeze

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + swing * depth * kSwayDrift
        character.rotation = swing * kSwayDegrees * mt.saturate(depth * 3.0)

        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, ctx.char_count) * kFadeStagger
        local appear = mt.ease.out_quad(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local vanish = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        character.opacity = appear * (1.0 - vanish)
    end
end
description: Showcase: tanzaku telop. Each vertical column hangs like a paper strip tied at its top: the whole strip swings gently in a slow breeze, and the swing grows with hanging depth -- the top character barely moves while the bottom one drifts the most, with a slight phase delay traveling down the strip like a wave along the paper. Columns swing on their own phases (line_index), so the strips never move in lockstep. Quiet enough for long-running captions; intro and outro are fades.

name: 47_vertical_smoke.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5
-- @recommend lang ja pos 0.5 0.85 bg #1e1e1e
-- Showcase: incense-smoke telop. Vertical text materializes the way
-- smoke climbs: each character rises into its spot from below, swaying
-- on noise that dies away as it settles, in reading order down the
-- columns. While the text holds, a whisper of the sway remains. At the
-- outro the smoke lets go -- every character drifts upward, swaying
-- harder and thinning out until the column has dispersed.

local kIntroDuration = 1.2 -- seconds
local kOutroDuration = 1.1 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.0 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kStaggerAmount = 0.55 -- reading-order cascade across characters
local kRiseDistance = 0.12 -- canvas fraction climbed during the intro
local kDisperseDistance = 0.16 -- canvas fraction drifted up during the outro
local kSwayAmount = 0.018 -- canvas fraction of the smoke sway while loose
local kIdleSwayAmount = 0.002 -- residual sway while settled
local kSwaySpeed = 0.6 -- sway noise time scale
local kDisperseStretch = 0.25 -- vertical thinning while dispersing

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    ctx.global.text = "ゆらゆらと\nたちのぼる"
    ctx.global.vertical = true
    ctx.global.v_align = "top"
    ctx.global.line_spacing = 1.2
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local stagger = mt.distribute(index, math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)) * kStaggerAmount
        local settle = mt.ease.out_cubic(mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))
        local disperse = mt.ease.in_quad(mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger))

        -- Loose = how smoke-like the character currently is: fully loose
        -- while rising and again while dispersing, near zero at rest.
        local loose = math.max(1.0 - settle, disperse)
        local swayStrength = kIdleSwayAmount + (kSwayAmount - kIdleSwayAmount) * loose
        local sway = mt.noise1(ctx.time * kSwaySpeed + index * 2.7, 71) * swayStrength

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + sway
        character.offset_y = 0.5 - (1.0 - settle) * kRiseDistance + disperse * kDisperseDistance
        character.stretch_y = 1.0 + disperse * kDisperseStretch
        character.opacity = settle * (1.0 - disperse)
    end
end
description: Showcase: incense-smoke telop. Vertical text materializes the way smoke climbs: each character rises into its spot from below, swaying on noise that dies away as it settles, in reading order down the columns. While the text holds, a whisper of the sway remains. At the outro the smoke lets go -- every character drifts upward, swaying harder and thinning out until the column has dispersed.

name: 48_chronos_time_dilation.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0

-- Showcase: Chronos Time Dilation
-- A unique relativistic time-dilation and pendulum-chronograph animation (completely distinct from 50):
-- 1. Intro (Chrono Release Arc): Characters swing in along circular pendulum arcs into position.
-- 2. Idle (Local Time Dilation & Breathing Stroke): Distance-dependent local time progression with dynamic stroke pulses and clock pendulum swings.
-- 3. Outro (Chrono Rewind Arc): Seamless pendulum time-reversal arc exit with zero stutter and normalized timeline.

local kIntroDuration = 1.0
local kOutroDuration = 0.8
local kStaggerInterval = 0.035
local kMaxOpacity = 1.0
local kTimeDilationStrength = 1.8
local kPendulumFrequency = 0.35
local kArcRadius = 0.14
local kBaseStrokeWidth = 0.015

local kColorTitanium = { r = 0.92, g = 0.94, b = 0.97, a = 1.0 }
local kColorCobaltStroke = { r = 0.28, g = 0.62, b = 0.95, a = 0.85 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local time = ctx.time
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration)

    -- Dynamic subtle spatial tilt
    ctx.global.yaw = mt.wave(time, 0.12, 0.0) * 3.0
    ctx.global.pitch = mt.wave(time, 0.15, 0.5) * 2.0

    -- Global opacity blending
    ctx.global.opacity = mt.ease.out_cubic(introProgress) * (1.0 - outroProgress)
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local time = ctx.time
    local remainingTime = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx)
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration)
    local totalChars = ctx.char_count

    -- Ensure bounding box is disabled to remain completely distinct from 50
    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = false

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local geometry = character.geometry

        -- Relativistic Local Time Dilation based on distance from center
        local dx = geometry.bounds_center_x - 0.5
        local dy = geometry.bounds_center_y - 0.5
        local distFromCenter = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
        local localTime = time * (1.0 + (distFromCenter - 0.2) * kTimeDilationStrength)

        -- 1. Intro: Pendulum Arc Release
        local charIntroRaw = mt.clamp((localTime - (index - 1) * kStaggerInterval) / 0.45, 0.0, 1.0)
        local charIntroEased = mt.ease.out_cubic(charIntroRaw)
        local introRotation = (1.0 - charIntroEased) * -50.0
        local introArcX = (1.0 - charIntroEased) * -0.15
        local introArcY = (1.0 - charIntroEased) * -0.08

        -- 2. Outro: Pendulum Arc Rewind (Seamless normalized window)
        local staggerRatio = 0.03
        local charOutroWindowStart = (index - 1) * staggerRatio
        local charOutroWindowSpan = math.max(0.3, 1.0 - (totalChars - 1) * staggerRatio)
        local charOutroRaw = mt.clamp((outroProgress - charOutroWindowStart) / charOutroWindowSpan, 0.0, 1.0)
        local charOutroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(charOutroRaw)
        local outroRotation = charOutroEased * 50.0
        local outroArcX = charOutroEased * 0.15
        local outroArcY = charOutroEased * -0.08

        -- 3. Idle: Pendulum Oscillation & Breathing Time Dilation Stroke
        local pendulumPhase = index * 0.35
        local pendulumAngle = math.sin(localTime * kPendulumFrequency * math.pi * 2.0 + pendulumPhase) * 0.18
        local idleArcX = math.sin(pendulumAngle) * kArcRadius
        local idleArcY = (1.0 - math.cos(pendulumAngle)) * kArcRadius * 0.5

        -- Dynamic localized stroke pulsation symbolizing time distortion
        local strokePulse = (mt.wave(localTime * 1.2, 0.6, distFromCenter * 4.0) * 0.5 + 0.5) * 0.015
        character.stroke.use = true
        character.stroke.width = kBaseStrokeWidth + strokePulse
        character.stroke.color = kColorCobaltStroke

        -- Composite transformations (Circular Arc + Rotation)
        character.offset_x = 0.5 + introArcX + outroArcX + idleArcX
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + introArcY + outroArcY + idleArcY
        character.rotation = introRotation + outroRotation + math.deg(pendulumAngle)
        character.pivot_y = 0.8 -- Pivot anchored near bottom for natural pendulum swing
        character.opacity = mt.clamp(charIntroEased * (1.0 - charOutroEased), 0.0, kMaxOpacity)

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = kColorTitanium
    end
end

name: 49_antigravity_singularity.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5.0
-- @required 3d
-- @recommend bg #040509

-- Showcase: Quantum Zero-G Field
-- The signature animation of Antigravity:
-- 1. Intro: Parts smoothly emerge from a central singularity using fluid spring dynamics (mt.spring).
-- 2. Idle: Deep space platinum base with quantum OKLCH cyan fluctuations and multi-octave zero-G drift (mt.wiggle).
-- 3. Outro: Grid deconstruction into 3D space with normalized seamless timeline and zero stutter.

local kIntroDuration = 1.2
local kOutroDuration = 0.9
local kStaggerInterval = 0.03
local kSpringFrequency = 2.2
local kSpringDamping = 3.5
local kZeroGAmplitude = 0.018
local kMaxOpacity = 1.0

local kColorDeepSpace = { r = 0.88, g = 0.90, b = 0.94, a = 1.0 }
local kColorCyanTint = { r = 0.25, g = 0.85, b = 0.95, a = 1.0 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local time = ctx.time
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration)

    -- Gentle anti-gravitational spatial posture rotation
    ctx.global.rotation = mt.wave(time, 0.12, 0.0) * 1.5
    ctx.global.yaw = mt.wave(time, 0.15, 0.5) * 4.0
    ctx.global.pitch = mt.wave(time, 0.18, 1.0) * 2.5

    -- Global opacity blending
    ctx.global.opacity = mt.ease.out_cubic(introProgress) * (1.0 - outroProgress)
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local time = ctx.time
    local remainingTime = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx)
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration)
    local instanceSeed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local totalParts = ctx.part_count

    for index = 1, ctx.part_count do
        local part = ctx.parts[index]
        local geometry = part.geometry

        -- 1. Intro: Physical spring fluid transition from singularity
        local staggerTime = (index - 1) * kStaggerInterval
        local introTime = time - staggerTime
        local introProgressPart = mt.clamp(introTime / 0.5, 0.0, 1.0)
        local springSettle = mt.spring(introTime, kSpringFrequency, kSpringDamping)

        local dx = 0.5 - geometry.canvas_center_x
        local dy = 0.5 - geometry.canvas_center_y
        local introOffsetX = 0.5 + dx * springSettle
        local introOffsetY = 0.5 + dy * springSettle
        local introZ = springSettle * 1.5
        local introScale = mt.lerp(0.1, 1.0, mt.ease.out_expo(introProgressPart))

        -- 2. Outro: Grid Deconstruction (seamless normalized window)
        local staggerRatio = 0.025
        local partOutroWindowStart = (index - 1) * staggerRatio
        local partOutroWindowSpan = math.max(0.3, 1.0 - (totalParts - 1) * staggerRatio)
        local partOutroRaw = mt.clamp((outroProgress - partOutroWindowStart) / partOutroWindowSpan, 0.0, 1.0)
        local partOutroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(partOutroRaw)

        local gridDirection = (index % 2 == 0) and 1.0 or -1.0
        local outroOffsetX = partOutroEased * 0.1 * gridDirection
        local outroZ = partOutroEased * -0.8
        local outroYaw = partOutroEased * 90.0 * gridDirection

        -- 3. Idle: Zero-G Multi-octave Drift & Quantum Spectrum
        local wiggleX = mt.wiggle(time, 0.35, kZeroGAmplitude, 2, instanceSeed + index)
        local wiggleY = mt.wiggle(time, 0.28, kZeroGAmplitude * 1.2, 2, instanceSeed + index * 2)
        local driftZ = mt.wave(time, 0.3, index * 0.2) * 0.02

        local distFromCenter = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
        local rippleHue = mt.wrap(time * 0.2 + distFromCenter * 1.5, 0.0, 1.0)
        local oklchColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.78, 0.18, rippleHue, 1.0)
        local quantumPulse = (mt.wave(time * 1.5, 0.6, distFromCenter * 3.0) * 0.5 + 0.5) * 0.3
        local finalColor = mt.color.lerp(kColorDeepSpace, oklchColor, quantumPulse)

        -- Composite transform
        part.offset_x = introOffsetX + outroOffsetX + wiggleX
        part.offset_y = introOffsetY + wiggleY
        part.z = introZ + outroZ + driftZ
        part.yaw = outroYaw
        part.scale = introScale * (1.0 - partOutroEased * 0.4)
        part.opacity = mt.clamp(introProgressPart * (1.0 - partOutroEased), 0.0, kMaxOpacity)

        part.fill.use = true
        part.fill.color = finalColor
    end
end

name: 50_architectural_kinetic_typography.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 4.0

-- Showcase: Architectural Kinetic Typography
-- A minimalist, sophisticated typographic animation prioritizing precision, typography, and elegance:
-- 1. Intro: Cinematic wide tracking collapse (mt.ease.out_expo) into precise grid alignment with sharp bounding box.
-- 2. Idle: Elegant monochrome aesthetic with subtle camera dolly and breathing tracking motion.
-- 3. Outro: Sharp linear slide and geometric clipping fade out.

local kIntroDuration = 1.0
local kOutroDuration = 0.8
local kWideTrackingStart = 0.45
local kNormalTracking = 0.0
local kMaxOpacity = 1.0
local kBoxMargin = 120.0
local kBoxWidth = 12.0
local kBoxCornerRadius = 4.0
local kCameraZoomMin = 1.0
local kCameraZoomMax = 1.05
local kBreathFrequency = 0.3

local kColorTextNormal = { r = 0.92, g = 0.93, b = 0.95, a = 1.0 }
local kColorBoxStroke = { r = 0.85, g = 0.86, b = 0.88, a = 0.85 }
local kColorBoxFill = { r = 0.12, g = 0.13, b = 0.16, a = 0.4 }

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local time = ctx.time
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration)

    -- Dynamic wide tracking collapse to normal grid pitch
    local introTrackingProgress = mt.ease.out_expo(introProgress)
    local introTracking = mt.lerp(kWideTrackingStart, kNormalTracking, introTrackingProgress)
    local outroTracking = outroProgress * 0.15
    local breathTracking = mt.wave(time, kBreathFrequency, 0.0) * 0.015
    ctx.global.tracking = introTracking + outroTracking + breathTracking

    -- Subtle camera dolly for cinematic depth
    local cameraZoom = mt.lerp(kCameraZoomMin, kCameraZoomMax, mt.ease.in_out_sine(introProgress))
    ctx.camera.zoom = cameraZoom + mt.wave(time, 0.25, 0.0) * 0.01

    -- Smooth global opacity control
    local introOpacity = mt.clamp(introProgress * 2.0, 0.0, kMaxOpacity)
    local outroOpacity = 1.0 - outroProgress
    ctx.global.opacity = introOpacity * outroOpacity
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local time = ctx.time
    local remainingTime = mt.timeline.remaining(ctx)
    local introProgress, outroProgress = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration)

    -- Architectural Bounding Box configuration
    ctx.bounding_box.enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.width = kBoxWidth
    ctx.bounding_box.color = kColorBoxStroke
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_enabled = true
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_color = kColorBoxFill
    ctx.bounding_box.fill_opacity = 0.4 * (1.0 - outroProgress)
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_x = kBoxMargin * (0.8 + 0.2 * mt.ease.out_cubic(introProgress))
    ctx.bounding_box.margin_y = kBoxMargin * 0.6
    ctx.bounding_box.corner_radius = kBoxCornerRadius
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_top = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_bottom = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_left = true
    ctx.bounding_box.draw_right = true

    -- Character-level linear slide and smooth staggered outro
    local totalChars = ctx.char_count
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local staggerRatio = 0.04

        -- Intro character vertical slide (smooth drop-in)
        local charIntroRaw = mt.clamp((time - (index - 1) * 0.03) / 0.35, 0.0, 1.0)
        local charIntroEased = mt.ease.out_cubic(charIntroRaw)
        local introOffsetY = (1.0 - charIntroEased) * -0.06

        -- Outro character horizontal slide (seamless staggered motion anchored to outroProgress)
        -- Normalizing window so all characters finish smoothly before clip end without sudden stop
        local charOutroWindowStart = (index - 1) * staggerRatio
        local charOutroWindowSpan = math.max(0.3, 1.0 - (totalChars - 1) * staggerRatio)
        local charOutroRaw = mt.clamp((outroProgress - charOutroWindowStart) / charOutroWindowSpan, 0.0, 1.0)
        local charOutroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(charOutroRaw)
        local outroOffsetX = charOutroEased * 0.12

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + introOffsetY
        character.offset_x = 0.5 + outroOffsetX
        character.opacity = charIntroEased * (1.0 - charOutroEased)

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = kColorTextNormal
    end
end

name: 51_ripple_echo.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 5.5
-- Showcase: concentric ripple echo. A ring-shaped shockwave expands from
-- the text's geometric center; each character reacts when the wave front
-- reaches it -- a brief lift, a scale pop, and a cool-to-warm color flash
-- -- then settles with a soft after-ripple. Because the driver is each
-- character's radial distance from the center (not its index), the wave
-- visibly travels through multi-line layouts as a circle rather than a
-- left-to-right cascade.
--
-- The intro is the first expanding front that "wakes" every glyph; the
-- idle phase keeps a slower second harmonic for a living surface; the
-- outro reverses the ring so glyphs sink back into stillness from the
-- outside in.

local kIntroDuration = 1.1 -- seconds for the first wake front to finish
local kOutroDuration = 0.85 -- seconds
local kFallbackClipLength = 5.5 -- seconds, used when ctx.timeline is unavailable
local kWakeRadius = 0.55 -- canvas units the intro front travels past center
local kWaveSpeed = 0.42 -- canvas units per second of the idle harmonic
local kWaveWidth = 0.07 -- half-width of the ring's gaussian envelope
local kLiftHeight = 0.045 -- canvas-height fraction at peak crest
local kScalePop = 0.22 -- extra scale at the crest
local kIdleAmplitude = 0.55 -- relative strength of the continuous harmonic
local kBaseHue = 0.55 -- cyan resting hue
local kFlashHue = 0.08 -- warm flash hue at the crest

local function gaussian(distance, width)
    return math.exp(-(distance * distance) / (width * width))
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local aspect = ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio

    -- Intro front starts collapsed at the center and expands outward.
    local introFront = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount) * kWakeRadius
    -- Idle harmonic keeps a slow ring pinging forever after the wake.
    local idleFront = mt.cycle(ctx.time, kWakeRadius / kWaveSpeed) * kWakeRadius
    -- Outro front collapses from the outside back to the center.
    local outroFront = (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount)) * kWakeRadius

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local geometry = character.geometry
        local worldX = (geometry.bounds_center_x - 0.5) * aspect
        local worldY = geometry.bounds_center_y - 0.5
        local radius = math.sqrt(worldX * worldX + worldY * worldY)

        local introCrest = gaussian(radius - introFront, kWaveWidth)
        local idleCrest = gaussian(radius - idleFront, kWaveWidth) * kIdleAmplitude * introAmount
        local outroCrest = gaussian(radius - outroFront, kWaveWidth) * outroAmount

        -- Characters "wake" once the intro front has passed them, and
        -- fall back asleep as the outro front reclaims them from outside.
        local woken = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kWaveWidth * 1.5, introFront - radius)
        local asleep = mt.smoothstep(0.0, kWaveWidth * 1.5, radius - outroFront)
        local presence = woken * (1.0 - asleep * outroAmount)

        local crest = introCrest + idleCrest + outroCrest
        local lift = crest * kLiftHeight
        -- Outro also gently sinks the whole line so the exit is not only a
        -- ring fade but a physical collapse.
        local sink = outroAmount * 0.03

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + lift - sink
        character.scale = 1.0 + crest * kScalePop
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(presence * 1.15) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroAmount) * 0.35)

        local flash = mt.saturate(introCrest + idleCrest * 0.6)
        local restingColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kBaseHue, 0.35, 0.92, 1.0)
        local flashColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kFlashHue, 0.75, 1.0, 1.0)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(restingColor, flashColor, flash)
    end
end

Because the driver is each character's radial distance from the center (not its index), the wave visibly travels through multi-line layouts as a circle rather than a left-to-right cascade.

name: 52_curious_lean.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0
-- @required 3d
-- Showcase: Grok's "maximum curiosity" lean-in (3D).
-- Explicit three-block structure:
--   1. Intro  — glyphs peer in from the wings with a skeptical side-tilt,
--               like someone leaning into a conversation they weren't
--               invited to (staggered, out_back snap).
--   2. Steady — continuous "thinking" idle: alternating micro head-tilts,
--               a sly amber pulse through the fill, and a slow yaw drift
--               as if re-reading the room. Never settles into stillness.
--   3. Outro  — irreverent shrug-off: each glyph spins on its heel, tosses
--               a wink (scale pulse) and exits the opposite wing.
--
-- Personality cue: curious, a little rude, never corporate-smooth.
-- Distinct from hinge_swing (single hinge slam) and orbit_reveal (orbit
-- arrival) — this is character-level attitude acting, not geometry gags.

local kIntroDuration = 1.15
local kOutroDuration = 0.95
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kStaggerAmount = 0.5
local kWingDistance = 0.28 -- canvas fraction slid in from the side
local kPeekDrop = 0.04 -- slight drop while peeking in
local kIntroTiltDegrees = 18.0
local kSteadyTiltDegrees = 5.5
local kSteadyTiltFrequency = 0.55 -- Hz, thinking nod cadence
local kSteadyYawDegrees = 7.0
local kSteadyPulse = 0.06 -- scale breath while thinking
local kOutroSpinDegrees = 55.0
local kOutroKick = 0.34 -- canvas fraction of the exit shove
local kAmberHue = 0.08
local kSteelHue = 0.58

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local steadyAmount = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount))

    -- Room re-read: slow global yaw only while thinking.
    ctx.global.yaw = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.11, 0.0) * kSteadyYawDegrees * steadyAmount
    ctx.global.pitch = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.09, 1.2) * 2.0 * steadyAmount
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)
        local stagger = order * kStaggerAmount

        -- Per-character block weights (each finishes before clip end).
        local introRaw = mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local outroRaw = mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local introEased = mt.ease.out_back(introRaw)
        local outroEased = mt.ease.in_back(outroRaw)
        local introClamped = mt.saturate(introEased)
        local steadyWeight = introClamped * (1.0 - outroEased)

        -- Wing side alternates so the lean-in reads as a crowd, not a march.
        local wingSign = ((index % 2) == 0) and 1.0 or -1.0
        local personality = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.75, 1.25)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 1. Intro: side-eye peek from the wings
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local introRemain = 1.0 - introClamped
        local introOffsetX = wingSign * kWingDistance * introRemain * personality
        local introOffsetY = -kPeekDrop * introRemain
        local introRotation = -wingSign * kIntroTiltDegrees * introRemain
        local introOpacity = mt.saturate(introRaw * 2.2)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 2. Steady: thinking tilts + sly amber pulse (never still)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local thinkPhase = ctx.time * kSteadyTiltFrequency * math.pi * 2.0
            + index * 0.85
            + personality
        local thinkTilt = math.sin(thinkPhase) * kSteadyTiltDegrees * steadyWeight * personality
        local thinkNod = math.sin(thinkPhase * 0.5 + 0.4) * 0.008 * steadyWeight
        local thinkPulse = 1.0
            + math.sin(thinkPhase * 1.3) * kSteadyPulse * steadyWeight
        local amberMix = (math.sin(thinkPhase * 0.7) * 0.5 + 0.5) * steadyWeight * 0.55

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 3. Outro: heel-spin shrug and opposite-wing exit
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local outroOffsetX = -wingSign * kOutroKick * outroEased * personality
        local outroOffsetY = kPeekDrop * 0.6 * outroEased
        local outroRotation = wingSign * kOutroSpinDegrees * outroEased
        local wink = 1.0 + math.sin(outroEased * math.pi) * 0.18
        local outroFade = 1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outroRaw)

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + introOffsetX + outroOffsetX
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + introOffsetY + thinkNod + outroOffsetY
        character.rotation = introRotation + thinkTilt + outroRotation
        character.scale = thinkPulse * wink
        character.opacity = introOpacity * outroFade

        local steel = mt.color.from_hsv(kSteelHue, 0.18, 0.92, 1.0)
        local amber = mt.color.from_hsv(kAmberHue, 0.72, 1.0, 1.0)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(steel, amber, amberMix)
    end
end

Never settles into stillness.   3. Outro  — irreverent shrug-off: each glyph spins on its heel, tosses               a wink (scale pulse) and exits the opposite wing.

name: 53_neural_spark.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0
-- Showcase: Grok's "chaos → answer → punchline" neural spark.
-- Explicit three-block structure:
--   1. Intro  — pure static: glyphs scatter as noisy half-formed thoughts
--               (random offset / rotation / desync opacity), then a single
--               decisive "click" of order snaps them onto the baseline
--               with a spring — the moment the model commits to an answer.
--   2. Steady — electric wit idle: OKLCH hue crawls along the line like a
--               thought current, each character ticks a tiny vertical
--               "token" hop on its own phase, stroke width breathes as if
--               voltage is running through the type.
--   3. Outro  — punchline scatter: the answer detonates into high-energy
--               fragments (new random rays, spin, scale pop) — not a
--               reverse of the intro, but a different joke exit.
--
-- Personality cue: xAI / Grok energy — chaotic intelligence that lands
-- clean, then refuses a polite fade. Distinct from part_assemble
-- (part geometry burst), glitch (quantized corruption), and cosmic_dust
-- (soft stardust dock): this is character-level "thought → reply → mic
-- drop" acting with a voltage palette.

local kIntroDuration = 1.25
local kOutroDuration = 1.0
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kStaggerAmount = 0.48
local kChaosMin = 0.14
local kChaosMax = 0.38
local kChaosSpin = 140.0
local kSpringFrequency = 3.6
local kSpringDamping = 3.4
local kTokenHop = 0.012 -- canvas fraction of steady token ticks
local kTokenFrequency = 1.4 -- Hz base for token hops
local kStrokeBase = 0.01
local kStrokePulse = 0.012
local kPunchDistance = 0.42
local kPunchSpin = 200.0
local kPunchScale = 0.45

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local steadyAmount = mt.ease.out_cubic(introAmount) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outroAmount))

    -- Thought-current tracking: slightly tight while answering, looser
    -- in chaos / punchline so fragments can breathe.
    ctx.global.tracking = mt.lerp(0.06, 0.0, steadyAmount)
    ctx.global.shadow.enabled = true
    ctx.global.shadow.distance = 1.0 + (1.0 - steadyAmount) * 0.8
    ctx.global.shadow.angle = 110.0
    ctx.global.shadow.color = { r = 0.05, g = 0.15, b = 0.35, a = 0.55 }
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed
    local time = ctx.time

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)
        local stagger = order * kStaggerAmount

        local introRaw = mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local outroRaw = mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local outroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroRaw)

        -- Spring commit: scatterWeight 1 = pure chaos, 0 = locked answer.
        local springTime = introRaw * 1.2
        local springSettle = mt.spring(springTime, kSpringFrequency, kSpringDamping)
        local scatterWeight = mt.lerp(1.0, springSettle, mt.saturate(introRaw * 10.0))
        local answerWeight = mt.saturate(1.0 - scatterWeight) * (1.0 - outroEased)
        local steadyWeight = answerWeight

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 1. Intro: noisy half-thoughts → decisive spring commit
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local chaosAngle = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local chaosDistance =
            mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount, kChaosMin, kChaosMax)
        local chaosSpin =
            mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount * 2, -kChaosSpin, kChaosSpin)
        local introOffsetX = math.cos(chaosAngle) * chaosDistance * scatterWeight
        local introOffsetY = math.sin(chaosAngle) * chaosDistance * scatterWeight
        local introRotation = chaosSpin * scatterWeight
        -- Flicker while uncommitted, solid once the spring locks.
        local chaosFlicker = 0.35
            + 0.65 * mt.random_range(seed + math.floor(time * 18.0), index, 0.0, 1.0)
        local introOpacity = mt.lerp(chaosFlicker, 1.0, mt.saturate(1.0 - scatterWeight))

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 2. Steady: voltage current + per-glyph token hops
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local tokenPhase = time * kTokenFrequency * math.pi * 2.0
            + order * math.pi * 1.7
            + mt.random_range(seed, index + 7, 0.0, math.pi)
        -- Soft square-ish hop: mostly down, brief uptick = "token emit".
        local tokenWave = math.max(0.0, math.sin(tokenPhase))
        local tokenHop = tokenWave * tokenWave * kTokenHop * steadyWeight
        local voltage = (mt.wave(time, 0.85, order * 2.4) * 0.5 + 0.5) * steadyWeight
        local currentHue = mt.wrap(0.52 + order * 0.22 + time * 0.08, 0.0, 1.0)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 3. Outro: punchline detonation (new rays, not intro reverse)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local punchAngle =
            mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount * 3, 0.0, math.pi * 2.0)
        local punchSpin =
            mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount * 4, -kPunchSpin, kPunchSpin)
        local punchOffsetX = math.cos(punchAngle) * kPunchDistance * outroEased
        local punchOffsetY = math.sin(punchAngle) * kPunchDistance * outroEased
        local punchRotation = punchSpin * outroEased
        local punchScale = 1.0 + kPunchScale * outroEased
        local punchFade = 1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroRaw)

        character.offset_x = 0.5 + introOffsetX + punchOffsetX
        character.offset_y = 0.5 + introOffsetY + tokenHop + punchOffsetY
        character.rotation = introRotation + punchRotation
        character.scale = punchScale
        character.opacity = introOpacity * punchFade

        -- Voltage palette: ice → electric cyan/violet while answering,
        -- blows toward hot white on the punchline.
        local answerColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.78 + voltage * 0.1, 0.16 + voltage * 0.08, currentHue, 1.0)
        local chaosColor = mt.color.from_oklch(0.55, 0.04, 0.6, 1.0)
        local punchColor = { r = 1.0, g = 0.95, b = 0.88, a = 1.0 }
        local filled = mt.color.lerp(chaosColor, answerColor, answerWeight)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(filled, punchColor, outroEased)

        character.stroke.use = true
        character.stroke.width = kStrokeBase + kStrokePulse * voltage
        character.stroke.color = mt.color.from_oklch(0.7, 0.14, currentHue, 0.35 + voltage * 0.5)
        character.stroke.gap = 0.0

        character.shadow.use = true
        character.shadow.color = {
            r = 0.1,
            g = 0.35,
            b = 0.9,
            a = 0.1 + 0.35 * answerWeight,
        }
    end
end

Steady — electric wit idle: OKLCH hue crawls along the line like a               thought current, each character ticks a tiny vertical               "token" hop on its own phase, stroke width breathes as if               voltage is running through the type.   3. Outro  — punchline scatter: the answer detonates into high-energy               fragments (new random rays, spin, scale pop) — not a               reverse of the intro, but a different joke exit.

name: 54_comet_arc.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0
-- Showcase: comet arc path (mt.path.bezier + mt.path.catmull_rom).
-- Explicit three-block structure driven by closed-form curves, not
-- frame-to-frame simulation:
--   1. Intro  — each character streaks in along its own cubic Bezier
--               (offset-space, neutral 0.5 = natural seat). Rotation
--               follows the path tangent so glyphs read as comets, not
--               sliding cards.
--   2. Steady — a small Catmull-Rom figure-eight patrol around the seat,
--               still tangent-aligned, with a cool spectral trail color.
--   3. Outro  — a different Bezier exit (new control points, not a
--               reverse of the intro) that flings glyphs off-frame.
--
-- Control points are in offset units (canvas-normalized displacement;
-- 0.5 is zero motion). See API §10.7. Distinct from orbit_reveal /
-- vortex_spiral (circular z/spin gags) — this is pure path evaluation.

local kIntroDuration = 1.2
local kOutroDuration = 0.95
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kStaggerAmount = 0.55
local kSteadyRadius = 0.018 -- figure-eight half-size in offset space
local kSteadyPeriod = 2.8 -- seconds per full idle loop
local kTrailHue = 0.55

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)
    local seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)
        local stagger = order * kStaggerAmount

        local introRaw = mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local outroRaw = mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local introEased = mt.ease.out_cubic(introRaw)
        local outroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroRaw)

        -- Per-glyph wing and height so the cascade fans out.
        local wingSign = ((index % 2) == 0) and 1.0 or -1.0
        local entryLift = mt.random_range(seed, index, 0.12, 0.22)
        local entrySide = wingSign * mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount, 0.18, 0.32)
        local exitSide = -wingSign * mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount * 2, 0.22, 0.38)
        local exitDrop = mt.random_range(seed, index + characterCount * 3, -0.08, 0.12)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 1. Intro: Bezier comet arrival (path progress 0 → 1)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local introP0 = { x = 0.5 + entrySide, y = 0.5 + entryLift }
        local introP1 = { x = 0.5 + entrySide * 0.35, y = 0.5 + entryLift * 0.15 }
        local introP2 = { x = 0.5 - wingSign * 0.04, y = 0.5 - 0.02 }
        local introP3 = { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 }
        local introX, introY, introTangentX, introTangentY =
            mt.path.bezier(introP0, introP1, introP2, introP3, introEased)
        local introRotation = math.deg(math.atan(introTangentY, introTangentX))

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 2. Steady: Catmull-Rom figure-eight around the seat
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local loopProgress = mt.cycle(ctx.time + order * 0.35, kSteadyPeriod)
        local idleWaypoints = {
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 },
            { x = 0.5 + kSteadyRadius, y = 0.5 + kSteadyRadius * 0.55 },
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 },
            { x = 0.5 - kSteadyRadius, y = 0.5 - kSteadyRadius * 0.55 },
            { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 },
        }
        local idleX, idleY, idleTangentX, idleTangentY =
            mt.path.catmull_rom(idleWaypoints, loopProgress)
        local idleRotation = math.deg(math.atan(idleTangentY, idleTangentX)) * 0.35

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 3. Outro: different Bezier exit (not intro reversed)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local outroP0 = { x = 0.5, y = 0.5 }
        local outroP1 = { x = 0.5 + exitSide * 0.25, y = 0.5 + 0.06 }
        local outroP2 = { x = 0.5 + exitSide * 0.7, y = 0.5 + exitDrop * 0.4 }
        local outroP3 = { x = 0.5 + exitSide, y = 0.5 + exitDrop }
        local outroX, outroY, outroTangentX, outroTangentY =
            mt.path.bezier(outroP0, outroP1, outroP2, outroP3, outroEased)
        local outroRotation = math.deg(math.atan(outroTangentY, outroTangentX))

        -- Pick the active block pose (do not cross-lerp path samples —
        -- that would leave the curve). Outro wins, then intro, else idle.
        local pathX = idleX
        local pathY = idleY
        local rotation = idleRotation
        if outroEased > 0.0 then
            pathX = outroX
            pathY = outroY
            rotation = outroRotation
        elseif introEased < 1.0 then
            pathX = introX
            pathY = introY
            rotation = introRotation
        end

        character.offset_x = pathX
        character.offset_y = pathY
        character.rotation = rotation
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(introRaw * 2.5) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroRaw))
        character.scale = 1.0 + (1.0 - introEased) * 0.2 + outroEased * 0.15

        -- Cool comet trail palette; brighter while still airborne on the arc.
        local airAmount = (1.0 - introEased) + outroEased
        local baseColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kTrailHue + order * 0.08, 0.35, 0.88, 1.0)
        local hotColor = mt.color.from_hsv(kTrailHue - 0.08, 0.55, 1.0, 1.0)
        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = mt.color.lerp(baseColor, hotColor, mt.saturate(airAmount))
    end
end
description: Showcase: comet arc path (mt.path.bezier + mt.path.catmull_rom). Explicit three-block structure driven by closed-form curves, not frame-to-frame simulation:   1. Intro  — each character streaks in along its own cubic Bezier               (offset-space, neutral 0.5 = natural seat). Rotation               follows the path tangent so glyphs read as comets, not               sliding cards.   2. Steady — a small Catmull-Rom figure-eight patrol around the seat,               still tangent-aligned, with a cool spectral trail color.   3. Outro  — a different Bezier exit (new control points, not a               reverse of the intro) that flings glyphs off-frame.

name: 55_storyboard_keys.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0
-- Showcase: storyboard keyframes (mt.keyframes).
-- Explicit three-block structure written as closed-form key tables
-- rather than nested clamp / inverse_lerp chains:
--   1. Intro  — multi-beat entrance on a per-character local clock
--               (drop → bounce → settle) with a warm color ramp.
--   2. Steady — a short looping keyframe phrase (lift / tilt / hue)
--               evaluated on a cycled time base so the hold never
--               freezes into a dead pose.
--   3. Outro  — a separate key table for crouch → launch → fade, with
--               a cool exit tint. Not a reverse of the intro keys.
--
-- Number keys drive offset / scale / rotation; a parallel color key
-- table drives fill. Both are pure mt.keyframes calls — the point of
-- this sample is to show multi-segment choreography without hand-rolled
-- segment math. See API §10.5 and reference/18_mt_keyframes.lua.

local kIntroDuration = 1.25
local kOutroDuration = 1.0
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kStaggerSeconds = 0.07 -- real-time cascade between characters
local kSteadyLoopSeconds = 1.6

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)
        -- Real-second stagger (not progress-scaled) so typing speed stays
        -- constant when the clip is stretched.
        local localTime = ctx.time - (index - 1) * kStaggerSeconds

        local introRaw = mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + order * 0.45) - order * 0.45)
        local outroRaw = mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + (1.0 - order) * 0.4) - (1.0 - order) * 0.4)
        local introEased = mt.ease.out_cubic(introRaw)
        local outroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroRaw)
        local steadyWeight = introEased * (1.0 - outroEased)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 1. Intro keys: drop → bounce → settle (localTime seconds)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local introOffsetY = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 0.18 },
            { t = 0.4, v = 0.0, ease = "out_bounce" },
            { t = 0.85, v = 0.0 },
        }, localTime)
        local introScale = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 0.55 },
            { t = 0.35, v = 1.08, ease = "out_back" },
            { t = 0.7, v = 1.0, ease = "out_cubic" },
        }, localTime)
        local introRotation = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = -18.0 },
            { t = 0.45, v = 4.0, ease = "out_cubic" },
            { t = 0.8, v = 0.0, ease = "in_out_sine" },
        }, localTime)
        local introColor = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = { r = 0.35, g = 0.4, b = 0.55, a = 1.0 } },
            { t = 0.5, v = { r = 1.0, g = 0.72, b = 0.35, a = 1.0 }, ease = "out_cubic" },
            { t = 0.95, v = { r = 0.92, g = 0.93, b = 0.96, a = 1.0 }, ease = "in_out_sine" },
        }, localTime)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 2. Steady keys: looping phrase on a cycled clock
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local steadyClock = mt.cycle(ctx.time + order * 0.25, kSteadyLoopSeconds) * kSteadyLoopSeconds
        local steadyOffsetY = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 0.0 },
            { t = 0.4, v = 0.012, ease = "in_out_sine" },
            { t = 0.9, v = -0.006, ease = "in_out_sine" },
            { t = kSteadyLoopSeconds, v = 0.0, ease = "in_out_sine" },
        }, steadyClock)
        local steadyRotation = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 0.0 },
            { t = 0.5, v = 3.5, ease = "in_out_sine" },
            { t = kSteadyLoopSeconds, v = 0.0, ease = "in_out_sine" },
        }, steadyClock)
        local steadyScale = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 1.0 },
            { t = 0.55, v = 1.04, ease = "in_out_sine" },
            { t = kSteadyLoopSeconds, v = 1.0, ease = "in_out_sine" },
        }, steadyClock)
        local steadyColor = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = { r = 0.92, g = 0.93, b = 0.96, a = 1.0 } },
            { t = 0.7, v = { r = 0.55, g = 0.78, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }, ease = "in_out_sine" },
            { t = kSteadyLoopSeconds, v = { r = 0.92, g = 0.93, b = 0.96, a = 1.0 }, ease = "in_out_sine" },
        }, steadyClock)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 3. Outro keys: crouch → launch (outro-local seconds)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- Map outroRaw 0–1 onto a fixed 0–1 second key window so the
        -- phrase always completes at clip end regardless of clip length.
        local outroClock = outroEased * 1.0
        local outroOffsetY = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 0.0 },
            { t = 0.25, v = -0.02, ease = "in_cubic" },
            { t = 1.0, v = 0.28, ease = "in_back" },
        }, outroClock)
        local outroScale = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 1.0 },
            { t = 0.3, v = 0.88, ease = "in_cubic" },
            { t = 1.0, v = 1.25, ease = "in_cubic" },
        }, outroClock)
        local outroRotation = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = 0.0 },
            { t = 1.0, v = 22.0 * (((index % 2) == 0) and 1.0 or -1.0), ease = "in_cubic" },
        }, outroClock)
        local outroColor = mt.keyframes({
            { t = 0.0, v = { r = 0.92, g = 0.93, b = 0.96, a = 1.0 } },
            { t = 0.45, v = { r = 0.75, g = 0.55, b = 1.0, a = 1.0 }, ease = "out_cubic" },
            { t = 1.0, v = { r = 0.25, g = 0.3, b = 0.55, a = 1.0 }, ease = "in_cubic" },
        }, outroClock)

        -- Block composite: intro pose → steady phrase → outro launch.
        local offsetY = introOffsetY
        local scale = introScale
        local rotation = introRotation
        local fillColor = introColor

        offsetY = mt.lerp(offsetY, steadyOffsetY, steadyWeight)
        scale = mt.lerp(scale, steadyScale, steadyWeight)
        rotation = mt.lerp(rotation, steadyRotation, steadyWeight)
        fillColor = mt.color.lerp(fillColor, steadyColor, steadyWeight)

        offsetY = mt.lerp(offsetY, outroOffsetY, outroEased)
        scale = mt.lerp(scale, outroScale, outroEased)
        rotation = mt.lerp(rotation, outroRotation, outroEased)
        fillColor = mt.color.lerp(fillColor, outroColor, outroEased)

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + offsetY
        character.offset_x = 0.5
        character.scale = scale
        character.rotation = rotation
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(introRaw * 3.0) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroRaw))

        character.fill.use = true
        character.fill.color = fillColor
    end
end
description: Showcase: storyboard keyframes (mt.keyframes). Explicit three-block structure written as closed-form key tables rather than nested clamp / inverse_lerp chains:   1. Intro  — multi-beat entrance on a per-character local clock               (drop → bounce → settle) with a warm color ramp.   2. Steady — a short looping keyframe phrase (lift / tilt / hue)               evaluated on a cycled time base so the hold never               freezes into a dead pose.   3. Outro  — a separate key table for crouch → launch → fade, with               a cool exit tint. Not a reverse of the intro keys.

name: 56_inspector_knobs.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @duration 6.0
-- Showcase: inspector knobs hack — tune script coefficients from the host UI.
--
-- Why this works
-- --------------
-- Every frame, ctx is rebuilt from the HOST INSPECTOR (and its keyframes)
-- before callbacks run. Script writes apply for that frame only and never
-- write back. The next frame the host values arrive again. So you can:
--   1. READ a parameter as a coefficient
--   2. OVERWRITE it (or drive characters from it) with the animation
--
-- Pure knobs vs dual-use
-- ----------------------
-- Rotation: read then overwrite the same field in OnPreLayout (sway). The
-- slider no longer means a static pose — only amplitude.
-- Scale: if left alone, host Scale still resizes the whole text. For a pure
-- "travel strength" knob we read it, force scale back to 1.0, then use the
-- number in OnLayout. OnLayout only sees post-OnPreLayout ctx, so the
-- coefficient is parked for this frame on gradient.angle while color_space
-- stays "none" (no gradient drawn). That is same-frame handoff, not storage
-- across frames — the host still resends Scale every frame.
-- Tracking / Line spacing: left dual-use (also affect layout metrics).
--
-- MT Sim: prefer always-visible Global fields. Shadow Distance needs
-- "Draw shadow" on before it is editable.
--
-- Knob map:
--   Tracking      → cascade stagger (also letter-spacing; try 0.2 … 0.4)
--   Rotation      → sway amplitude degrees (try 0 … 25; base sway always on)
--   Scale         → intro travel only (size forced to 1; try 0.6 … 1.6)
--   Line spacing  → idle bob (try 0.5 … 2.5)
--
-- Blocks: staggered pop-in → wave/bob hold → reverse cascade exit.

local kIntroDuration = 1.1
local kOutroDuration = 0.9
local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
local kBaseWaveDegrees = 4.0
local kBaseStagger = 0.05
local kBaseRise = 0.07
local kBaseBob = 0.01

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    -- Rotation → pure sway amplitude (read, then overwrite same field).
    local waveAmplitudeDegrees = kBaseWaveDegrees + ctx.global.rotation
    ctx.global.rotation = mt.wave(ctx.time, 0.22, 0.0) * waveAmplitudeDegrees

    -- Scale → pure travel coefficient: capture, neutralize size, hand off
    -- to OnLayout via inactive gradient.angle (gradient stays off).
    local scaleKnob = ctx.global.scale
    if scaleKnob < 0.05 then
        scaleKnob = 0.05
    end
    ctx.global.scale = 1.0
    ctx.global.gradient.color_space = "none"
    ctx.global.gradient.angle = scaleKnob
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introAmount, outroAmount =
        mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, kIntroDuration, kOutroDuration, kFallbackClipLength)
    local characterCount = math.max(ctx.char_count, 1)

    local staggerAmount = mt.clamp(kBaseStagger + ctx.global.tracking, 0.0, 0.6)
    -- Scale knob recovered from same-frame handoff (size already forced to 1).
    local scaleKnob = ctx.global.gradient.angle
    if scaleKnob < 0.05 then
        scaleKnob = 0.05
    end
    local lineSpacingKnob = ctx.global.line_spacing
    if lineSpacingKnob < 0.05 then
        lineSpacingKnob = 0.05
    end

    local riseAmount = kBaseRise * scaleKnob
    local bobAmount = kBaseBob * lineSpacingKnob

    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local character = ctx.chars[index]
        local order = mt.distribute(index, characterCount)
        local stagger = order * staggerAmount

        local introRaw = mt.saturate(introAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local outroRaw = mt.saturate(outroAmount * (1.0 + stagger) - stagger)
        local introEased = mt.ease.out_back(introRaw)
        local outroEased = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroRaw)
        local steadyWeight = mt.saturate(introEased) * (1.0 - outroEased)

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 1. Intro: staggered pop from below (rise from Scale knob)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local introOffsetY = (1.0 - mt.saturate(introEased)) * riseAmount
        local introScale = mt.lerp(0.72, 1.0, mt.saturate(introEased))

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 2. Steady: phase bob (Line spacing knob)
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local phase = order * math.pi * 2.0 + ctx.time * 1.7
        local bob = math.sin(phase) * bobAmount * steadyWeight
        local twist = math.sin(phase * 0.55) * 4.0 * steadyWeight

        ------------------------------------------------------------
        -- 3. Outro: reverse cascade drop
        ------------------------------------------------------------
        local outroOffsetY = -outroEased * riseAmount * 1.1

        character.offset_y = 0.5 + introOffsetY + bob + outroOffsetY
        character.offset_x = 0.5
        character.scale = introScale * (1.0 - outroEased * 0.15)
        character.rotation = twist
        character.opacity = mt.saturate(introRaw * 2.5) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_quad(outroRaw))
    end
end
